title: VoluCompose: Constructing Compact Volumetric Visual Representations for Medical Image Understanding
summary: Medical vision--language models can interpret volumetric images, but processing full volumes is costly because hundreds of slices produce long, redundant visual-token sequences. Existing compression methods often couple content selection with budget determination. We observe that neighboring slices share visual features and that attention concentration varies across visual encoders. We propose VoluCompose, a training-free, model-agnostic framework that separates what visual content to retain from how many tokens to allocate. Its hyperbolic token composition module groups contiguous slices into ordered support units and uses the Lorentz distance to account for feature magnitude and direction during token allocation, anchor selection, and refinement. Its capacity control module uses visual-encoder attention entropy to allocate more tokens when attention is more dispersed. We evaluate VoluCompose on two tasks across three datasets and four backbones. Across nine calibrated settings, VoluCompose attains the highest mean quality--retention hypervolume among the compared methods. It achieves a mean relative quality of 121.68\% against the uncompressed references while retaining 22.78% of visual tokens on average. Compression remains robust even at a 10% token budget. Across settings, the lowest ROUGE-L ratio to the uncompressed reference is 96.4\% for VoluCompose. The corresponding minima for the compression baselines range from 15.0% to 70.5%. Code is available at https://github.com/yezanting/VoluCompose.

title: Scoring, Not Learning: Decomposing Catalog-Consolidation Gains in Web-Scraped Retail Product Recognition
comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, was accepted by a computer vision conference workshop
summary: Retail product catalogs assembled from web image search are cheap to build and pervasively noisy: queries return packaging shots instead of products, and entries proliferate under names that cannot be distinguished visually. Consolidating such a catalog can look like an alternative to scaling the model. We show this is not a comparison between two ways of improving a recognizer, but between improving a recognizer and changing what counts as correct. We study a public archive of 165,769 cheese images across 1,824 query-named entries. A packaging filter and near-duplicate removal reduce it to a 998-class recognition set on one fixed, group-aware split. Canonicalizing entries to their base type (844 classes) raises top-1 accuracy by 4.0 points. Scoring the unchanged model against the merged label space, by summing its predicted probability within each canonical group, recovers +4.27 points with no retraining (+4.25 over six seeds). Retraining on the consolidated catalog then adds -0.10$\pm$0.53, +0.08$\pm$0.65 and -0.10$\pm$0.65 points at 28, 50 and 88 M parameters, indistinguishable from zero at every capacity ($\pm$ is the across-seed standard deviation). That component is specific, not mechanical: random merges with the identical size profile yield only +0.68 points, and the three backbones agree to within 0.1 points. But it is overwhelmingly category coarsening, not alias correction: across the 37 merged groups, type coarsenings supply 94% of the gain and alias collapses only 7%. We also detect no interaction between consolidation and backbone size: tripling backbone parameters is worth +1.50$\pm$0.57 points on the raw catalog and +1.42$\pm$00.44 on the canonical one, a within-seed interaction of -0.08 [-0.79,+0.63]. On this archive, the reported consolidation gain primarily reflects the evaluation label space, and separating that out costs one evaluation

title: JEPAhead: From Inpainting to Causal Forecasting for Urban Driving
summary: We fine-tune a pre-trained V-JEPA1 predictor from bidirectional latent inpainting to action-free causal forecasting while keeping the encoder frozen. Using contiguous past observations, horizon-aligned targets, and group-level causal attention, the model forecasts eight future token groups, corresponding to sixteen frames, in one forward pass. On CARLA Town12, it retrieves the correct future among 591 candidates in 69.0% of cases, compared with 55.3% for persistence, with greater gains at longer horizons and on tokens exhibiting greater change. It also outperforms a compact predictor trained from scratch with six times fewer parameters. Semantic analysis indicates driving-relevant information in predicted features: a fixed linear probe trained on real encoder tokens achieves 0.16 mIoU on patches undergoing semantic-class changes, versus 0.13 for persistence. Vehicle-conditioned retrieval improves over persistence by 15 percentage points at the longest horizon. Pixel-space evaluation shows modest L1 gains but little improvement under LPIPS, motivating direct evaluation through latent and semantic measures alongside an oracle reconstruction reference. These findings support further investigation of latent forecasting for driving perception, while downstream utility remains unverified.

title: AtariBench: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in Atari Gameplay
comment: 26 pages, 14 figures. Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on static visual understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to act in dynamic environments remains less well understood. We introduce AtariBench, a controlled benchmark that evaluates VLMs across 20 Atari 2600 games, requiring models to make sequential decisions from high-temporal-resolution gameplay streams. By decoupling fast in-game dynamics from wall-clock inference speed, AtariBench focuses on whether models can perceive rapid visual state changes, reason over spatiotemporal dynamics, and ground actions in the current observation. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs: models often fail to infer object motion and direction, exhibit brittle sequential decision-making, and over-rely on textual interaction history despite newly appended visual feedback. We further introduce a separability analysis to identify which in-game scores provide reliable signals of model competence, and use the benchmark to study how memory design and prompting strategies affect performance. Overall, AtariBench exposes a persistent gap between passive visual perception and active decision-making, providing a lightweight and rigorous testbed for developing VLMs that can reason and act in dynamic environments.

title: Federated training performs as well as centralized for 3D Latent Diffusion for Diagnosis-Conditioned Brain MRI Synthesis
summary: Generative models of brain MRI are useful to understand brain conditions, and to enrich scarce and imbalanced neuroimaging data. However, training these models requires large, multi-site training sets, which is challenging. Federated learning (FL) allows for training deep learning models without sharing data. We show that training a 3D conditional latent model federatedly (where data is kept private at each site) performs similarly to centralized training (where all the data have been copied to a single site). We evaluate three metrics: conditional fidelity (how well generated MRIs perform in classification), diversity (how the generated images match the real data distribution, using MultiScale-SSIM), and realism (how close generated images are to real images, using Fréchet Inception Distance). Our results show that federated training is a viable route to develop multi-site generative models of brain MRI.

title: LEF-JEPA: Denoising-Trained Latent Energy Fields for Spatial Representation Learning
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 7 tables. Includes supplementary material
summary: A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that applies prediction supervision only at masked positions struggles to clearly capture object shapes and boundaries in its latent representations. We further observe that some existing methods improve spatial structure while also retaining rich variations in texture and color. However, preserving more low-level visual information does not necessarily make representations better suited to prediction and action. This raises a key question: how can we strengthen the spatial structure in latent representations that supports prediction and action without over-encoding these details? We introduce LEF-JEPA, which learns spatial structure through target-guided latent recovery and transfers this supervision to the visual encoder through a relative-energy constraint; the energy module is used only during pretraining and adds no inference overhead. To reduce the cost of energy optimization during pretraining, we further construct a conditional Ising Hamiltonian that allows low-energy-state search to be performed by specialized Ising solvers. On physical hardware, we validate the feasibility of achieving lower forward latency with fewer local updates. Under a unified CIFAR-10 pretraining and frozen-encoder evaluation protocol, both realizations outperform V-JEPA2.1 in image classification, foreground segmentation, and visual planning.

title: Seeing vs. Counting: Complexity Twins Show Where Multimodal LLMs Fail on Diagrams
comment: 8 pages main text + 96 pages appendix (107 pages in total, including references)
summary: When a multimodal LLM miscounts in a diagram, does it fail at seeing or at counting? Existing visual graph and puzzle benchmarks vary visual density and algorithmic hardness together, confounding the two. We pair counting questions about the same drawing that sit in different counting-complexity classes, such as its spanning trees (a determinant) and its simple paths (#P-complete), and use a transcription probe and a text-only control to separate reading from computing. We test Gemini, Gemma and Qwen3-VL models; for the Gemini models, the answer depends on how the model computes. In chain of thought, most of them read small drawings correctly and then fail at counting, at a rate set far more by the size of the answer than by its complexity class (for the primary model, the odds of an exact answer fall 2.38-fold per decade of the answer). Given code and an exact transcription, the primary model counts correctly even on 10x10 grids, and reading becomes the bottleneck: a single view misses horizontal edges, and a second reading of a rotated copy with crop checks reads 86/96 large grids exactly, against 57/96 when the upright reading is simply repeated.

title: Did I See It or Think It? Probing Reality Monitoring in Vision-Language Models with Concept Injection
summary: Recent work tests whether language models can introspect by injecting a concept direction into their activations and asking whether they notice it and can name it. These studies are text-only. Vision-language models (VLMs) face an additional problem, known in cognitive psychology as reality monitoring: they must keep internally generated content separate from what they actually see. We therefore ask: can VLMs distinguish injected concepts from image content? We introduce a paradigm that varies the image and the injected concept independently. On each trial, the model reports what it sees, whether a thought was injected, and what that thought is. This design scores both whether the model identifies the concept and which source it assigns to it. Across six VLMs, only Gemma-3-27B reliably identifies injected concepts (35% vs. 3% for steering alone), with almost no false alarms. Even then, the source it reports is fragile. Strong or visual-pathway injections are reported as seen, and a visible object nearly eliminates correct thought reports. The same failure appears in ordinary captioning, where injected objects appear in up to 87% of captions of real photographs. Evaluating multimodal self-reports therefore requires checking both their content and their reported source.

title: ProtoCouncil: Multi-Encoder Anatomical Prototypes for Prostate Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound
summary:
Purpose: Micro-ultrasound ($μ$US) is a promising modality for prostate cancer (PCa) detection, but identifying suspicious tissue depends heavily on clinical experience. Models trained on sparse, noisy core-level pathology offer little insight into their decisions and can fail under domain shift. Clinical use needs a traceable decision process and a flag for uncertain predictions.
  Methods: We introduce ProtoCouncil, in which three foundation encoders (MedSAM, DINOv3 and V-JEPA 2.1) learn case-based prototypes at three anatomical levels: whole gland, needle track and gland sectors. Prototypes are projected onto real training-core regions, and label-free fusion keeps every class logit as a bias plus an exact sum of prototype similarity contributions. Encoder disagreement triggers selective prediction.
  Results: In five-fold patient-level cross-validation (6,588 cores, 693 patients), ProtoCouncil reaches 82.9% AUROC for clinically significant PCa (csPCa, Grade Group $\geq$3), 4.3 points above the best previously published method. In zero-shot evaluation on two external cohorts, ProtoCouncil achieves higher all-cancer and csPCa AUROC than all previous methods. Nearest same-class exemplars match test-core tumor involvement better than random same-class cases. Externally, csPCa accuracy falls from 79% when encoders agree to 27% when two oppose the fused call. Abstaining on disagreement raises balanced accuracy by 7 and 15 points, while retaining 58% and 54% of the cores.
  Conclusion: ProtoCouncil grounds core-level predictions in exact similarity-based evidence from real, anatomically indexed training cases, which makes its reasoning interpretable. It achieves the highest csPCa AUROC across three cohorts and identifies unreliable predictions through encoder disagreement.

title: UniRGBA: Unifying RGB and Alpha in Pretrained Video Diffusion Models
summary: Recent advances in video diffusion models have achieved remarkable photorealistic RGB synthesis, yet generating videos with a native alpha channel remains an open challenge. Existing approaches often rely on matting-style data and non-native RGBA designs, causing them to specialize in real-object scenes and to degrade severely on visual-effect content whose semi-transparency is spatially non-local and non-elliptical. We present UniRGBA, a unified framework whose key insight is that RGBA generation does not require a dedicated alpha encoder or complex latent-space restructuring---a minimal, targeted extension of the existing RGB pathway is sufficient. UniRGBA-VAE extends a causal video VAE to 4-channel RGBA via zero-initialized channel expansion, symmetric selective layer unfreezing (5% trainable), and a six-term progressive reconstruction loss anchored by a KL reference loss that prevents latent drift, followed by a two-stage schedule that introduces a lightweight GAN objective. We then apply standard DoRA to the pretrained DiT, reusing the unified 4-channel latent without any alpha-specific architectural changes. On a visual-effect RGBA benchmark, UniRGBA substantially outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA reconstruction while preserving RGB fidelity. For generation, UniRGBA outperforms Wan-Alpha on RGBA text-to-video tasks and matches or surpasses the original pretrained Wan2.1 backbone on RGB-only metrics, demonstrating that native alpha support can be integrated without compromising the underlying RGB prior or the model's architectural versatility.

title: GlobalPuzzle: Globally Informed Genetic Search for Eroded Jigsaw Puzzle Reassembly
comment: 22 pages (10 pages main paper and 12 pages supplementary material), 16 figures
summary: Jigsaw puzzle reassembly remains a highly challenging task, particularly when piece boundaries are irregularly eroded to simulate damage to cultural artifacts. On the GAP benchmark, existing methods achieve a perfect assembly accuracy of only 0.3% on $5 \times 5$ puzzles, whereas humans can solve jigsaw puzzles with remarkably high accuracy. Humans typically approach puzzle solving by identifying potentially adjacent pieces, evaluating the current assembly, and iteratively performing complex operations such as adding pieces, replacing incorrectly placed pieces, and moving entire connected groups of pieces. However, existing methods face a fundamental limitation: approaches that leverage global visual information typically predict piece arrangements directly, making it difficult to explicitly perform such complex iterative operations, while search based methods can rearrange pieces but primarily rely on pairwise boundary compatibility, lacking global visual information to evaluate and guide the search process. To bridge this gap, we propose GlobalPuzzle, a jigsaw puzzle reassembly framework that integrates global canvas level evaluation, action guidance, and genetic search. By incorporating global visual information into the evaluation and optimization of candidate assemblies, GlobalPuzzle aims to resolve ambiguous adjacency relationships that are difficult to determine from irregularly eroded piece boundaries alone, enabling flexible, globally informed reconstruction.

title: Training-Free Active Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) for vision-language models (VLMs) is usually studied in a fully unsupervised regime, where adaptation relies on pseudo-labels, confidence scores, or entropy computed by the model itself. This is a severe restriction on hard shifted samples: the model is asked to repair its own uncertain predictions without any external evidence. At the other extreme, supervised online adaptation assumes labels can directly train or correct the model. We study the intermediate deployment regime between these two extremes. In Active Test-time Adaptation for VLMs (Active VLM-TTA), a pretrained VLM may spend an explicit labeling budget on selected test samples, but the prediction for the current sample must be emitted before its label can be used; queried labels are therefore costed, delayed evidence for future samples rather than free correction for the present one. Under this future-only constraint, the central question is how to reuse sparse labels conservatively. We instantiate this setting with ACTive VLM-TTA for Online Retrieval (ACTOR), a training-free plug-in module that routes uncertain samples among base prediction, label query, and memory-based correction using a consistency-and-reliability check over previously queried labels. Across ten cross-domain benchmarks and a domain-transfer benchmark based on ImageNet, ACTOR consistently improves strong VLM-TTA baselines on ResNet and ViT backbones with negligible inference overhead. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/kaist-dmlab/ACTOR.

title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering
summary: Long-video question answering forces multimodal large language models to reason under strict visual-token budgets, creating a tradeoff between broad temporal coverage and fine-grained spatial detail. Uniform sampling preserves coverage but often obscures decisive local cues, while caption-based or frame-similarity retrieval operates over lossy proxies that can miss motion, state changes, and before-after relations. We recast long-video reasoning as a visual-token allocation problem: given a fixed budget, decide how much to spend on global context versus high-resolution local evidence, and where in the video to draw that local evidence from. We introduce AdaAlloc, a training-free inference framework that adaptively allocates visual tokens between a global video overview and localized visual detail. AdaAlloc first plans a global/local allocation policy, then uses temporal grounding to locate candidate evidence segments and refines them into a compact temporal memory. The selected policy controls both frame sampling density and resolution, combining sparse, lower-resolution global frames with denser, higher-resolution local frames drawn from the refined memory. The final answerer reasons over the allocated global context and refined local evidence. Across LVBench, MLVU, VideoMME, and LongVideoBench, AdaAlloc improves over budget-matched uniform sampling by up to 10.5 percentage points and outperforms the compared frame-selection and agentic methods on their reported benchmarks.

title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection
summary: LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection (L3OD) is a fundamental 3D perception task, yet its performance is often compromised by domain shifts arising from diverse sensor configurations and environmental conditions. Existing Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) methods primarily leverage self-supervision in the spatial domain, yet they frequently confound semantic content with domain style due to the sparse, non-Euclidean nature of point clouds. To overcome this limitation, we propose FIND (Frequency INvariance Disentanglement), a novel TTA framework that precisely disentangles domain-invariant content from domain-specific interference within the frequency domain. Our methodology utilizes B-Spline fitting to construct locally adaptive filters integrated into a dual-stream architecture: an Invariant Stream extracts robust features to guide pseudo-labeling, while a Specific Stream enforces consistency against domain perturbations. By combining invariance-driven alignment with stability-guided regularization, our approach dynamically extracts robust domain-invariant features while suppressing domain-specific interference. Extensive experiments on cross-dataset adaptation and robust corruption benchmarks demonstrate that FIND significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/llldx03/FIND.

title: HMMF-Net: A Lightweight Hierarchical Multi-Frame Multimodal Fusion Network for Accurate Fish Feeding Intensity Assessment
summary: Automated fish feeding intensity assessment (FFIA) is important for precision aquaculture and feed cost optimization. However, unimodal methods are vulnerable to acoustic noise and visual disturbances, while existing multimodal frameworks often rely on computationally intensive 3D convolutions or Transformers, limiting their use on edge devices. To address these limitations, we propose HMMF-Net, a lightweight multimodal architecture that combines early multi-frame visual encoding and multi-axis acoustic modeling through a hierarchical bidirectional messenger cross-modal fusion (BMCF) mechanism. The visual branch captures temporal variations in feeding behavior by stacking temporally distant frames as a multi-channel input to an adapted 2D EfficientNetB0 backbone. The acoustic branch employs adaptive multi-axis residual units (AMARU) to extract temporal, frequency, and local time-frequency representations from log-mel spectrograms. BMCF progressively exchanges information between the two modalities at intermediate representation levels through compact messenger tokens, reducing the computational overhead of dense cross-modal attention. Evaluated on the AV-FFIA dataset using five-fold cross-validation, HMMF-Net achieves 96.77% accuracy and 96.88% F1-score on the held-out test folds, with 3.987M parameters and 1.002 GFLOPs. Compared with the best-performing visual configuration (95.49% accuracy), HMMF-Net reduces the classification error by 28.38%. Deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano using TensorRT with FP32 precision maintains comparable accuracy, with an inference time of 11.54 ms per 2-second sample and a model size of 18.81 MB. These results demonstrate that HMMF-Net combines effective multimodal representation learning with computational efficiency, enabling accurate and practical FFIA on resource-constrained edge platforms.

title: HiMEM: Hippocampus-Inspired Memory Consolidation, Pruning, and Composition for Vision-Language-Action Models in 3D Scenes
summary: Memory plays a crucial role in long-horizon task execution and cross-task generalization for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models operating in complex 3D scenes. However, existing VLA memory mechanisms suffer from memory noise, particularly in complex 3D scenes, as stored episodic memories contain extensive redundant details about scene layouts, object configurations, and robot-specific states, which obscure generalizable manipulation principles and hinder cross-task transfer. To address this challenge, we first introduce a hippocampus-inspired memory consolidation mechanism that synthesizes extensive episodic experiences into a compact set of essential semantic memories, enabling VLA models to derive generalizable principles from practical experience. Second, we propose an episodic memory pruning mechanism that removes redundant episodic memories whose contents are captured by consolidated semantic memories, thereby increasing effective memory capacity and improving long-horizon task execution. Finally, to handle complex task scenarios, we develop a flexible memory composition mechanism that jointly leverages multiple episodic and semantic memories to enhance cross-scenario generalization. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus demonstrate the effectiveness of HiMEM across different VLA backbones, improving the average success rate of pi_0 from 91.88% to 98.20% on LIBERO.

title: SPSC: Zero-Shot Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Reconstruction via Semantic Preservation and Subspace Calibration
summary: Pretrained vision-language models and diffusion generators have driven rapid progress in brain-to-image generation, while EEG-based reconstruction is still constrained by low signal-to-noise ratio and cross-subject semantic shifts. Zero-shot cross-subject reconstruction poses even greater challenges: EEG semantic embeddings learned from source subjects deviate from the manifold of image embeddings of the unseen target subject, particularly when neither target labels nor target image embeddings are available. To address this issue, we introduce the Semantic Preservation and Subspace Calibration (SPSC) framework, which first uses Object Mask Contrastive Regularization (OMCR) with object identity for backend training, and then constructs Subspace Candidate Gate (SCG) to achieve label-free semantic correction for target subjects during inference. Specifically, OMCR regularizes the conditioning space with object-level positive samples to preserve object-level feature neighborhoods within the reconstruction prior and low-level branch, while SCG exploits training image prototypes and batch statistics of unlabeled target EEG to select candidates for each task within subspaces of image prototypes. Under the leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) setting across ten subjects on the THINGS-EEG dataset, SPSC improves the cross-subject reconstruction from 0.552 to 0.713 on CLIP and from 0.612 to 0.745 on Alex.5. These significant gains indicate that the semantically calibrated conditions can better support generation for the target subjects under label-free inference.

title: FusionCLIP: Multimodal Contrastive Pretraining for Fusion Plasma Diagnostics
summary: Visible-light videos and multivariate diagnostic signals provide complementary observations of tokamak discharges. However, existing fusion pretraining methods, primarily learn representations by reconstructing or predicting observations, leaving the correspondence between these modalities underexplored. Representation learning is further challenged by the fact that plasma-related regions occupy only part of each video frame and diagnostic variables have substantially different sampling rates. We propose FusionCLIP, a multimodal contrastive pretraining framework. Spatiotemporal Stability Selection retains informative visual tokens, while a Temporal Query Encoder integrates asynchronous diagnostic signals using their observation timestamps. Contrastive learning then aligns the two modality representations. We construct EAST Multimodal Diagnostics (EAST-MMD), comprising 1307 EAST discharges, and evaluate the model on three independently fine-tuned tasks: disruption prediction, edge-localized mode (ELM) classification, and $H_{98}$ regression. FusionCLIP achieves an aggregate score of 89.07\%, exceeding the best general-purpose pretraining configuration and an in-domain contrastive pretraining configuration without Spatiotemporal Stability Selection by 6.27 and 2.12 percentage points, respectively. Ablations and attention visualizations further support the contributions of its key components.

title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
summary: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important for deploying evaluation metrics in real-world settings, where both input ambiguity and domain shifts are common. In this work, we propose an uncertainty-aware extension of the BEiTScore image captioning metric, producing conformally calibrated confidence intervals alongside alignment scores. Our approach models predictive distributions over human judgments, enabling both accurate scoring and principled uncertainty quantification in a single forward pass. We evaluate our BEiTScore++ metric across multiple benchmarks with human-annotated ratings, showing that it preserves the ranking correlation of BEiTScore, while producing intervals whose width tracks the prediction error more closely than Monte Carlo dropout on most benchmarks. The estimated uncertainty also grows under image degradation and on out-of-domain artwork images, making BEiTScore++ a practical tool for uncertainty-aware evaluation of image-caption alignment.

title: V-STORM: A Structure-Aware Grounded Chain of Thought Dataset for Faithful and Fine-Grained Spatio-Temporal Video Reasoning
summary: While MLLMs can often identify what happens in a video, they still struggle with fine-grained spatio-temporal reasoning, which requires precise grounding when and where the supporting evidence appears and composing such evidence into a coherent reasoning chain. This challenge is exacerbated by the lack of scalable data construction and evaluation pipelines that provide granular, verifiable supervision linking reasoning steps to explicit spatio-temporal evidence.To address this gap, we present V-STORM, a structure-aware framework that transforms videos into Spatio-Temporal Scene Graphs (STSGs) and derives Grounded Chain of Thought (GCoT) from validated evidence paths, making each reasoning step traceable to structured and verifiable spatio-temporal evidence.Under this framework, we construct a 260K-sample training set and a 3K-sample human-verified benchmark, both featuring GCoT annotations that link reasoning to explicit spatio-temporal evidence.Experiments reveal a clear separation between evidence localization and evidence composition: current MLLMs can often identify relevant spatio-temporal cues, yet still fail to integrate them into correct multi-step reasoning, exposing a bottleneck that answer-only evaluation largely obscures. Moreover, fine-tuning with V-STORM substantially improves both answer accuracy and grounding faithfulness, validating its effectiveness as supervision for faithful and evidence-grounded video reasoning. Our dataset, benchmark, and source code will be publicly released.

title: Multimodal Training with Knowledge Traction for Video Anomaly Detection
summary: The task of weakly supervised video anomaly detection is challenging. Existing approaches mainly model video frame features and determine whether anomalies are present based on their magnitudes. In this work, we propose a novel method that incorporates external knowledge into training to improve model performance, robustness, and generalization. We leverage textual prompts and a large language model (LLM) to establish prior information for the specific task, and employ dictionary learning to normalize and compress this information. Moreover, during experiments, we observed inconsistencies in the textual descriptions extracted from similar video frames by image caption models. To address this, we devise a method that leverages an LLM and auxiliary information to ensure consistency in the textual descriptions of similar frames within a video. Finally, we introduce a feature processing approach that incorporates prior knowledge and cross-modal attention mechanisms. This approach learns the relationships and characteristics among different modalities to construct more accurate and reliable feature representations, thereby improving the accuracy and stability of downstream tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses other state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
summary: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has been increasingly adopted to fine-tune pretrained models with low computational cost and is therefore also preferred in the federated learning paradigm to reduce computational and communication overhead. In this work, we investigate the sparsely explored problem of the risk of private data leakage in LoRA-adapted Vision Transformers (ViTs), where low-rank updates weaken the gradient signal available to a server with access to individual client updates. We show that quality of reconstruction is limited by two coupled ambiguities: reduced information in LoRA gradients and missing spatial cues from frozen positional embeddings. To address this, we propose a spatially anchored generative inversion framework that incorporates server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings into ViT blocks during fine-tuning at clients. The resulting positional gradients act as layer-wise spatial anchors, providing additional positional cues, while the generative prior keeps reconstructions on a realistic image manifold, reducing duplicate-data and patch-permutation artifacts, {which produce similar gradients as those produced when the target client images are used}. Adding our proposed spatial anchoring to GIAS improves PSNR by 10.14 dB, SSIM by 0.45, and LPIPS by 0.098 on CIFAR-10, as well as PSNR gains of 7.83 and 11.74 dB on high-resolution CelebA and CARS datasets, respectively, in the FedSGD setting. Such gains in reconstructed image quality metrics are also maintained at higher batch sizes and in FedAvg settings. These results indicate that LoRA-based PEFT does not, by itself, prevent data leakage in FL, and carefully incorporated positional embeddings can help in exposing private information.

title: GRAC: Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning for Surgical Scene Description
summary:
Purpose: Surgical operative reports support procedural documentation, surgical training, performance assessment, and workflow review. However, extracting meaningful information often requires extensive manual review and clinical expertise. Automated surgical scene descriptions could reduce this burden by leveraging recurring surgical activities and prior knowledge.
  Methods: We propose GRAC (Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Captioning), a framework that represents surgical scenes as graphs capturing relationships among instruments, actions, and anatomical structures. Given an input scene graph, GRAC learns to retrieve relevant graph-caption pairs from training data. It compares instrument-tissue interactions between retrieved examples and the input scene, using comparison features to condition retrieved-caption representations during generation.
  Results: On the EndoVis-18 benchmark, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.88, compared with 4.23 for SGT and 3.36 for the strongest conventional Transformer baseline. Exact instrument-action-target triplet-set accuracy reached 52.6%, compared with 32.7% for SGT and 26.2% for the strongest conventional baseline. These results demonstrate improvements in language quality and factual agreement. On TORS, GRAC achieved a CIDEr-D of 5.06, compared with 3.80 for the strongest baseline.
  Conclusion: GRAC demonstrates that combining structured surgical scene representations with retrieved examples improves surgical scene captioning and produces more contextually meaningful descriptions.

title: Assessing the detectability of standing dead trees in PlanetScope imagery
summary: Standing dead trees (SDTs) play a critical role in forest biodiversity assessment, disturbance monitoring, and carbon cycling. High-resolution optical satellite imagery offers an opportunity for large-scale SDT detection by providing finer spatial detail than moderate-resolution sensors. Despite this advantage, isolated SDTs may occupy only part of a PlanetScope pixel, allowing their signals to mix with those of live canopy, non-woody vegetation, and shadows. As a result, it is necessary to quantify signal detectability and detection stability across these conditions. To address this issue, this study uses PlanetScope imagery at 3 m resolution and Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-derived reference annotations to develop a multi-level, response-based SDT framework for analyzing SDT detectability from the aspect of the segmentation models, SDT density, and SDT patch sizes. UAV annotations are first aggregated to the PlanetScope pixel scale to generate hard labels and soft labels. The deep and machine learning models are then trained to select a stable reference semantic model and assess the consistency of SDT detection responses across architectures. All deep learning segmentation models produced consistent detectability responses, with HRNet achieving the best performance, with a binary F1 of 0.86. A single-pixel SDT signal became evident mainly when SDT cover proportion reached the 70 %-80 %, whereas neighborhood support lowered this change to a local SDT density of 20 %–30 %. Patch-level analysis indicated more stable detection for SDT patches larger than 90–180 m 2 . Furthermore, reliable PlanetScope detection is associated with SDT dominance, spatial aggregation, and high local SDT density . The proposed framework provides a detectability analysis approach for evaluating the stability of SDT detection in 3 m satellite imagery and the consistency of these responses across semantic segmentation models, linking high-resolution satellite imagery probability mapping with ultra-high-resolution UAV-based observations.

title: Satellite remote sensing of polar clouds: a review of cloud detection, phase identification, and microphysical property retrieval (2001–2025)
summary: Polar clouds play important roles in regulating the surface energy budget, atmospheric moisture cycle, precipitation, and sea-ice variability, while their occurrence, vertical structure, thermodynamic phase, and microphysical properties remain difficult to characterize consistently across the Arctic and Antarctic. Satellite remote sensing enables broad-scale monitoring of polar clouds, yet high-albedo snow and ice surfaces, weak cloud–surface thermal contrast, frequent temperature inversions, and persistent mixed-phase conditions make cloud detection and property retrieval substantially more difficult than at lower latitudes. This review synthesizes progress during the quarter-century 2001–2025 in polar cloud satellite remote sensing with a focus on satellite-based polar cloud detection, cloud phase identification, and microphysical retrieval. It first analyzes the synergistic monitoring capabilities of multi-source satellite sensors, including passive multispectral imagers, active radars and lidars, and microwave radiometers. It then explores in depth the evolution of cloud detection methods from static physical thresholds to deep learning algorithms that integrate spatial information and multimodal features. For cloud phase identification and microphysical retrieval, this paper reviews the physical principles and technical limitations of representative methods, including threshold and Lookup Table (LUT) methods, Optimal Estimation Method (OEM), variational and Bayesian retrievals, analytical and empirical methods, and machine-learning approaches, with particular attention to the challenges associated with ice–liquid phase partitioning and vertical heterogeneity in polar mixed-phase clouds. Finally, it identifies the deficiencies in current research regarding the application of far-infrared and high-frequency submillimeter-wave bands, the construction of full-spatiotemporal coverage observation networks, and the physical consistency of data-driven models, and outlines priorities for developing a continuous, multi-dimensional polar cloud monitoring system based on coordinated high- and low-orbit observations, recent and forthcoming satellite instruments, and physically constrained artificial intelligence.

title: A spatiotemporal difference-enhancement network with semantic flow alignment for fine-grained cropland change detection
summary: Accurate cropland change detection from high-resolution remote sensing images is essential for agricultural resource monitoring, land management, and food security. Existing methods struggle with two primary challenges: (1) severe pseudo-change noise and false alarms, caused by sole reliance on simple spatial or temporal difference enhancement, and (2) inadequate fine-grained cropland change detection, resulting from boundary detail degradation during fixed interpolation decoding. To address these issues, we propose a S patio T emporal D ifference- E nhancement N etwork (STDENet) with semantic flow alignment for effective cropland change detection from high-resolution remote sensing images. Built on a pyramid vision transformer V2 (PVT-V2) encoder, STDENet integrates three key innovations: a spatiotemporal dual-branch difference enhancement (STDDE) module that jointly captures temporal variations and spatial discrepancies to suppress irrelevant responses from unchanged or spectrally similar regions; an adaptive boundary-aware (ABA) module that dynamically extracts four-directional texture cues to enhance boundary representations; and a semantic flow-aligned decoding (SFAD) module that predicts semantic flow fields to warp high-level difference features and align them with low-level spatial details for fine-grained structure recovery. We evaluate the STDENet on one self-constructed dataset, DYCD, and two public benchmark datasets, CLCD and Hi-CNA. Comparative experiments confirm that STDENet consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods on all three datasets, improving IoU by 3.41 %, 4.90 %, and 1.98 % over the second-best methods on DYCD, CLCD, and Hi-CNA, respectively. By enhancing global structural information through the spatial branch and local change responses through the temporal branch, the spatiotemporal interaction design improves the feature separability of cropland changes. Semantic flow alignment helps restore fine-grained details by producing a more stable decoding process for local contours in cropland change patches. STDENet also demonstrates stronger resistance to interference and better adaptability to phenological variations among crop growth, pre-sowing, and post-harvest periods. Large-scale applications further indicate its generalization ability across heterogeneous cropland structures.

title: PHYIELD: Towards multi-scale maize yield estimation with limited ground reference data via integrated crop models and phenology-guided deep learning
summary: Accurately estimating crop yields across scales (e.g., regional administrative and field scales) is critical for global food security, given mounting challenges agriculture faces from climate change, population growth, soil degradation, and water scarcity. Remote sensing has been widely used for crop yield estimation with its spatially extensive coverage and temporally continuous observations of crop conditions. However, robust yield estimation across scales remains challenging, particularly under conditions of limited availability of crop yield and crop management data. While process-based crop models can capture complex interactions of plant-soil-atmosphere continuum, their large-scale application is limited by computational cost, parameterization difficulty, and model input (e.g., management) constraints. Empirical data-driven models are more flexible and computationally efficient, but they heavily depend on ground-measured yield labels that are often scarce over space and time. To address these challenges, we propose PHYIELD, a novel hybrid yield estimation framework that integrates systematically calibrated process-based crop modeling and phenology-guided deep learning for maize yield estimation at both county and field scales under yield data constraint conditions. PHYIELD mainly comprises three components: systematic crop model calibration, diversified crop model simulation, and phenology-guided deep learning. Given the challenges and prevalence of sparse yield observations in practice, PHYIELD is uniquely devised with limited ground yield records for model building. Its model performance is systematically evaluated for temporal, spatial, and scale transfers, upon comparison with standalone crop model and deep learning counterpart benchmarks. Results showed that the systematic crop model calibration of PHYIELD, particularly via the calibration for Leaf Area Index (LAI), followed by yield (biomass multiplied by Harvest Index [HI]), is essential for region-varying parameterizations of the crop model before coupling with deep learning. With diversified simulations from calibrated crop model and phenology-guided deep learning, PHYIELD achieved correlation (R) of 0.53–0.73, bias of −1.47–0.96 t ha⁻ 1 , and root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.07–1.68 t ha⁻ 1 in the study region, outperforming both crop model and deep learning benchmarks. Under significant yield data constraint condition (e.g., only 2023 county-level yield data of Illinois available), PHYIELD demonstrated superior temporal transferability over the preceding 20 year period (2003–2022) (R = 0.70, RMSE = 1.76 t ha⁻ 1 ), spatial transfer to surrounding states (R = 0.85, RMSE = 1.06 t ha⁻ 1 ), and scale transfer from county to field levels (R = 0.53–0.76, RMSE = 1.55–1.58 t ha⁻ 1 ). By leveraging the complementary strengths of process-based and data-driven modeling approaches, coupled with systematic parameterization of crop model and incorporation of phenology knowledge, PHYIELD provides a more robust and generalizable solution for multi-scale maize yield estimation, particularly under limited data conditions. It can largely support yield-oriented decision-making in agricultural management, policy development, and food security planning.

title: P2RBox: Point Prompt Oriented Object Detection with SAM
summary: Single-point annotation in oriented object detection of remote sensing scenarios is gaining increasing attention due to its cost-effectiveness.However, due to the granularity ambiguity of points, there is a significant performance gap between previous methods and those with fully supervision. In this study, we introduce P2RBox, which employs point prompt to generate rotated box (RBox) annotation for oriented object detection. P2RBox employs the SAM model to generate high-quality mask proposals. These proposals are then refined using the semantic and spatial information from annotation points. The best masks are converted into oriented boxes based on the feature directions suggested by the model. P2RBox incorporates two advanced guidance cues: Boundary Sensitive Mask guidance, which leverages semantic information, and Centrality guidance, which utilizes spatial information to reduce granularity ambiguity. This combination enhances detection capabilities significantly.To demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, enhancements based on the baseline were observed by integrating three different detectors. Furthermore, compared to the state-of-the-art point-annotated generative method PointOBB, P2RBox outperforms by about 29% mAP (62.43% vs 33.31%) on DOTA-v1.0 dataset,which provides possibilities for the practical application of point annotations.

title: A Domain-Specific Memory Bank-Enhanced Framework for Remote Sensing Image Captioning
summary: Remote sensing image captioning enables automated interpretation of remote sensing data for applications such as environmental monitoring and urban planning. However, general-purpose multimodal models exhibit suboptimal adaptability on remote sensing imagery due to domain discrepancies in data distribution, resolution, and rotation invariance. We propose a domain-specific memory bank-enhanced framework for remote sensing image caption, built upon the lightweight EVCap architecture with three core innovations: (1) a remote sensing specific visual memory bank providing domain-representative visual-semantic alignment; (2) a staged transfer training strategy that leverages pre-trained knowledge while mitigating overfitting from limited remote sensing data; and (3) a K-means clustering-based few-shot memory bank that preserves performance while reducing memory footprint for resource-constrained deployment. Extensive experiments on NWPU, RSICD, and Sydney datasets demonstrate substantial improvements over baselines. Specifically, CIDEr increases by 3.3% on RSICD (0.2735 to 0.2825) and 11.7% on Sydney (0.1422 to 0.1589). The proposed method also achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods while maintaining favorable computational efficiency.

title: Beyond Coastal Validation: Resolving Storm-Time Sea Surface Height Variability with SWOT High-Resolution Observations
summary: Coastal water levels during storms result from interacting tides, storm surges, waves, currents, bathymetry, and coastal geometry, producing spatially heterogeneous responses that remain difficult to characterize from point observations alone. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides a new opportunity to investigate this complexity through wide-swath High-Resolution (HR) observations of sea surface height (SSH). Here, SWOT HR water levels are first evaluated against five tide gauges in the English Channel and subsequently analyzed at three contrasting sites, Cherbourg, Villers-sur-Mer, and Étretat, using complementary spatial and scale-resolved approaches. SWOT HR shows strong agreement with tide gauges at the best-performing sites, with RMSE values of approximately 0.11 m and correlations exceeding 0.99, while accuracy remains site-dependent. Beyond point-based validation, the two-dimensional HR fields reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity, including localized and elongated SSH anomalies with distinct geometries and orientations. EOF decomposition shows that more than half of the variance remains beyond the first six modes at all three sites, highlighting the complexity of the HR spatial signal. The detrended SSH anomalies show organized spatial patterns, while their point-by-point linear correlations with radar backscatter (σ0) remain close to zero. Across the three investigated coastal domains and two storm events, the two-dimensional wavelet analysis identifies enhanced SSH variability within an energetic scale range of approximately 0.5–1.0 km, although its intensity, spatial distribution, and organization differ substantially among sites. Comparison with independent wave, surface-current, and bathymetric fields further places these observations within contrasting hydrodynamic and morphological environments, suggesting that the observed sub-kilometer SSH variability may be associated with local coastal processes, although their individual contributions remain unresolved. . Together, these analyses demonstrate the added value of SWOT HR for resolving the two-dimensional, multiscale complexity of storm-time coastal SSH, providing new spatial information for investigating coastal dynamics and supporting high-resolution model validation and data assimilation.

title: Sentinel-1 SAR Monitoring of River Water Surface Elevation: Effects of Wind, Waves, River Morphology and Vegetation
summary: Accurate monitoring of river water surface elevation (WSE) is important for hydrologic and flood applications, particularly where in situ observations are limited. This study evaluates Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for estimating river WSE using a river inundation area–water surface elevation (RIA–WSE) relationship derived from high-resolution topobathymetric elevation data and investigates environmental factors affecting estimation accuracy. A total of 265 Sentinel-1 SAR images acquired during 2015–2026 covering the USGS Thebes gauging station along the Mississippi River were analyzed using six VV- and VH-based backscatter metrics, yielding 1590 WSE estimates. Comparison with a conventional 1-m digital elevation model (DEM) revealed that its representation of river water-surface elevations at the time of the elevation survey, rather than submerged channel-bed elevations, limits its applicability for estimating WSE at low river stages. Among the six metrics, log10(VV) produced the best overall performance, with an RMSE of 1.61 m, mean error of −0.96 m, R2 of 0.81, and percentage of lowest absolute error (PLE) of 44.5%. A sensitivity analysis using SAR image grid spacings of 10, 5, 2, and 1 m showed that log10(VV) maintained relatively stable estimation accuracy, whereas finer resampling did not consistently improve WSE estimates. Errors were smallest under low-flow conditions (WSE < 97.0 m), largest under medium- to high-flow conditions (97.0–102.5 m) and decreased again during flooding (WSE > 102.5 m). Analysis of 10 National Agricultural Imagery Program (NAIP) images revealed increasing vegetation along the inundation boundary above approximately 100 m WSE. Under medium- to high-flow conditions, calm conditions generally produced smaller errors than non-calm conditions, although errors did not increase monotonically with wind speed. E–W and SE–NW wind orientations generally produced larger errors than N–S and NE–SW orientations. These results indicate that WSE estimation accuracy reflects combined effects of vegetation, wind-generated water surface roughness, wind orientation, effective fetch, water depth, and river morphology. Although log10(VV) performed best overall, it provided the lowest absolute error for only 44.5% of acquisitions, highlighting the potential for condition-dependent backscatter metric selection to improve SAR-based river WSE retrieval.

title: A Complex-Valued Multiscale Feature Interaction Attention Vision Transformer for PolSAR Image Classification with Amplitude–Phase Decoupling
summary: Limited labeled data and class imbalance complicate polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image classification. We propose a complex-valued multiscale feature interaction attention vision transformer (CV-MfIaViT) that combines spatial analytic-envelope preprocessing, complex-valued local feature extraction and global modeling. A two-dimensional Hilbert transform (2D HT) provides envelope features to the shallow pathway. The complex-valued amplitude–phase interaction attention (CV-APIA) module generates positive real gains through cross-modulation of pooled features; the final gating preserves the element-wise phase of non-zero input features. A complex-valued feature complementary mapper (CV-FCM), a complex-valued multiscale extractor (CV-MSE) and a complex-valued vision transformer (CV-ViT) complete the architecture. Under random-pixel sampling, the reported average accuracy (AA) exceeds CV-MsAtViT by 1.83, 3.42 and 2.48 percentage points on Flevoland, San Francisco and Nanjing, respectively. The advantage is also retained under spatial-block partitioning with shared label-free scene-level normalization. Component ablations and comparisons with two simple learned front ends characterize the combined design. The results support the evaluated architecture without isolating phase preservation as the cause of its accuracy gains.

title: Preliminary Overpass Level Assessment of Early NISAR 200 m L-Band Soil Moisture: Effects of Quality Control and Sensor Depth
summary: The NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission provides L-band soil moisture at 200 m, but validating its early products depends on retrieval flags, overpass collocation and sensor depth. We evaluated the beta Level-3 product against seven U.S. in situ networks (October 2025–January 2026) and the provisional product at 21 National Ecological Observatory Network sites (June–July 2026). Beta retrievals with flag 0, which averages all three candidate algorithms, were matched to in situ data within 60 min, merged by orbit and averaged over 0–10 cm sensors, yielding 261 site overpasses from 117 sites. Beta NISAR had a preliminary bias of 0.003 m3 m−3, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.081 m3 m−3 (95% interval 0.066–0.098) and R=0.578. Accepting all flag classes increased coverage ninefold and RMSE to 0.096 m3 m−3. On common site overpasses, deeper sensors did not have significantly higher RMSE than 5 cm sensors. The exploratory provisional assessment found a wet bias of 0.110 m3 m−3, concentrated at very dry reference sites, with a pooled R of −0.038 but an anomaly R within sites of 0.259. These estimates rest on few sites and short records; validation of early NISAR products should report flag classes, overpass construction and matched depths and separate pooled from temporal agreement.

title: SNAPxtra: An Open-Source Python Workflow for Automated Multi-Temporal InSAR Deformation Monitoring with SNAP
summary: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) is a satellite–based remote sensing technique capable of measuring surface displacement. However, InSAR measurements can be affected by temporal decorrelation, baseline geometry, and surface characteristics. Persistent scatterer (PS) and small baseline subset (SBAS) are two widely used multi-temporal InSAR techniques for addressing these limitations. Processing SAR acquisitions to derive deformation maps and displacement time series requires a series of complex steps. Many existing open-source and commercial software packages support PS or SBAS, while some support both methods, each with its own challenges and limitations. In this study, we presnet SNAPxtra, a Python-based InSAR automatic workflow to generate PS and SBAS interferometric stacks. These can be exported in the format required for time-series analysis in LiCSBAS and StaMPS. SNAPxtra has automated master selection, multi-swath and multi-frame processing, polygon-based masking, trial processing, and network generation features within an integrated workflow. The reproducibility and adaptability of SNAPxtra are demonstrated through case studies in Quetta (Pakistan), Surat (India), and Fort Worth (USA) as case studies using both PS and SBAS methods.

title: Satellite-Derived Landscape Characteristics Distinguish Streamflow Drought Occurrence
summary: The consequences of drought for rivers depend not only on the atmospheric water deficit but also on how catchments store and release water. It remains unclear how well catchment characteristics distinguish streamflow drought occurrence under similar meteorological conditions. We combined AlphaEarth satellite descriptors with principal component analysis to examine this question in 361 relatively undisturbed catchments across the conterminous United States. Using the three-month Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) and Standardized Streamflow Index (SSI), we linked meteorological droughts to subsequent streamflow droughts and assessed whether catchment landscapes helped explain differences in their occurrence, intensity and duration under comparable meteorological and initial streamflow conditions. Occurrence was most clearly associated with PC1, the dominant component of the AlphaEarth descriptors, whose landscape differences were partly reflected in drainage density and forest cover. At comparable meteorological drought durations and the same meteorological intensity and initial streamflow conditions, catchments in the upper PC1 quartile had estimated occurrence probabilities 8.1–20.9 percentage points below those in the lower quartile. The separation was greater for moderate-or-stronger drought, at 13.8–22.3 points. Higher PC1 also tended to accompany lower drought intensity, but the evidence for intensity and duration differences was less conclusive than for occurrence. These findings support the use of a common satellite-derived landscape description to identify catchments more susceptible to streamflow drought under comparable meteorological conditions, while showing that occurrence probability alone cannot indicate how severe or persistent the resulting drought will be.

title: Estimation of Radio Attenuation in Radiata Pine Canopy Using Aerial Lidar and Terrestrial GNSS
summary: Data from terrestrial GNSS receivers have been combined with point clouds from aerial lidar to estimate the average attenuation coefficients of foliage in planted pine forests at GNSS frequencies. The absorption and scattering of radio signals due to the presence of vegetation can degrade signals from communications and satellite-based navigation systems, making accurate estimates of attenuation essential for predicting equipment performance. Given the potentially limited ability of lidar to penetrate dense foliage, a method was developed to estimate the average attenuation of signals based on distance travelled beneath the maximum height envelope of tree canopies. This was accomplished by using aerial lidar data to determine the outer surface of the forest canopy based on the maximum height in each horizontal bin. Each GNSS satellite detection vector was then analysed to determine the total length traversed inside of the canopy envelope. Application to regions of planted radiata pine in a managed forest outside Adelaide, South Australia, yielded average attenuation coefficient estimates for satellites with a 30–60° elevation angle of 0.36 dB m−1 for 10-year-old medium-height and 0.35 dB m−1 for 19-year-old tall trees. The demonstrated method and results provide site and vegetation-type-specific data to inform predictive models of GNSS receiver performance at specific locations.

title: Applications of Deep Learning for Correcting Tropospheric Phase Delays in InSAR: A Review
summary: Tropospheric phase delay is a major error source that limits the accuracy of Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) deformation measurements, including those from the C- and X-band systems commonly examined in the studies reviewed here. Traditional correction methods, including external atmospheric models, spatiotemporal filtering, and phase–elevation empirical approaches, can partially mitigate atmospheric delays but often suffer from limited resolution, strong assumptions, or difficulties in separating atmospheric signals from complex surface deformation. Recent advances in deep learning provide new opportunities for InSAR tropospheric correction by learning nonlinear spatial and temporal relationships from interferometric observations and auxiliary information. This review provides a focused overview of deep learning-based approaches for correcting tropospheric phase delays in InSAR. Existing studies are organized according to their dominant modeling strategies, including convolutional neural network (CNN)-based spatial modeling, recurrent neural network (RNN)-based temporal modeling, generative adversarial network (GAN)-based generative learning, and other feedforward regression approaches. Key network-design strategies, training-label and dataset construction methods, and representative applications are discussed. Finally, current limitations and future research directions are discussed, emphasizing physical consistency, deformation preservation, cross-region generalization, and independent geodetic validation.

title: Ageing, Dilution and the Limits of Detection: A Canada-to-Romania Wildfire Smoke Transport Episode Observed with the RADO-Cluj ACTRIS National Facility and PACE Multi-Angle Polarimetry
summary: Smoke from the Canadian wildfires of August 2025 reached Cluj-Napoca, Romania, on 6–9 August as a thin layer at 5–8 km. We followed the plume from its source with the multi-angle polarimeters HARP2 and SPEXone and the OCI radiometer on NASA’s PACE and characterised it at the RADO-Cluj ACTRIS National Facility with a multiwavelength depolarisation lidar, a ceilometer, AERONET photometry, GRASP inversions, and HYSPLIT trajectories. Along the air mass trajectory, the HARP2 retrievals resolved the ageing of the smoke: an optical depth decaying from 0.9 to 0.2–0.3, a layer rising to 10 km and descending to 5 km, growth of the fine-mode radius, and a single-scattering albedo consistent with brown carbon loss. At the site, the lidar ratio and particle depolarisation ratio retrieved by HARP2 (52 sr, 0.042) agreed with the lidar’s derived lidar ratio and measured depolarisation (50 sr, 0.042), whereas the three satellite optical depths differed by 0.2 around an AERONET value of 0.1 and the NATALI typing networks returned three different classes. For this faint, aged plume, intensive polarimetric and vertical quantities could no longer be identified for the aerosol by its optical depth and Ångström exponent, which motivates testing an intensive-first pairing of satellite polarimetry with ground-based lidar on further episodes.

title: From Multi-Sensor Survey to a Multi-Scale Geospatial Digital Twin Foundation of a Historic Hill Town: Fiumefreddo Bruzio, Southern Italy
summary: Historic hill towns require geometric information capable of relating urban morphology, construction features, and structural details within a common spatial and semantic framework. This paper presents a multi-sensor, multi-scale geomatics workflow for establishing an integrated geospatial information framework for the historic centre of Fiumefreddo Bruzio in Calabria, southern Italy. A control network of 38 points provided the spatial reference for UAV and terrestrial photogrammetry, six SLAM trajectories, and 270 static laser scans covering five buildings. Point clouds generated by Structure from Motion and range-based sensors were co-registered in the RDN2008/UTM zone 33N coordinate reference system and used to produce orthophotos, digital terrain and surface models, contour lines, textured meshes, and building-scale drawings. These products were organised within an interoperable geospatial information system based on persistent links between settlement-, aggregate-, building-, façade-, space-, and macroelement-level entities. The framework also supported structural characterisation and seismic vulnerability assessment at building and urban scales, linking building screening and potential local mechanisms to their spatial interpretation. The resulting survey-based digital model supports conservation documentation, seismic screening, and street-network analysis, while providing the foundation for future digital twin development rather than an operational implementation. The study offers a transferable acquisition-to-information workflow, preserving data provenance and metric quality for risk-informed management of historic settlements.

title: Integrating Multi-Source Geospatial Data and Evaluating Model Architecture for Deep Learning-Based Flood Inundation Mapping
summary: Deep-learning research on flood inundation mapping is driven largely by architectural innovation and single-run reporting. We ask whether the segmentation architecture or the input representation contributes more to accuracy in flood-event surface-water mapping. We introduce GeoHybridNet, a hybrid CNN–Transformer network, and compare it on the hand-labeled Sen1Floods11 benchmark with a U-Net, an Attention U-Net, a parameter-matched wide U-Net, and SegFormer under matched data and training. The four convolutional and hybrid models differ by at most 1.4 IoU points, and none are significantly different under event-level tests; a compact SegFormer trained from scratch is about 3.5 points lower. In factorial designs crossing three architectures with up to five input representations (five seeds each), input representation explains about 95% of the variance in water IoU and architecture about 1%. The dominant input factor is radiometric normalization: raw bands standardized per chip reach only 60% IoU and adding NDWI restores 76%, whereas the same bands standardized with training-set statistics reach 77.5% without any index. The pattern holds when permanent water is excluded. On three held-out flood events, accuracy drops by 24–26 IoU points for every model. On this benchmark, input preparation and honest evaluation matter more than architecture.

title: Benchmarking Ten Machine-Learning Algorithms for Mediterranean Forest Mapping with Sentinel-2
summary: Accurate forest-cover mapping in fragmented Mediterranean landscapes remains challenging because forests, croplands, grasslands, and sparsely vegetated surfaces often exhibit overlapping spectral responses. This study benchmarks ten supervised machine-learning classifiers for regional forest-cover mapping in the Beni Mellal-Khenifra region of Morocco, evaluates the contribution of spectral, textural, and topographic predictors, and assesses the consistency of the resulting forest map with the Hansen Global Forest Change product. A reference dataset of 2800 samples representing forest, crops/grass, bare ground, urban areas, and water was combined with an annual 2025 Sentinel-2 median composite, spectral indices, NDVI-derived gray-level co-occurrence matrix textures, and SRTM-derived elevation and slope. The samples were divided once into a stratified 70% training set and a 30% test set common to all classifiers. Redundancy, correlation (|r| > 0.80), and variance inflation factor (VIF < 10) screening, fitted on the training set only, reduced 56 candidate predictors to 16, and hyperparameters were tuned by five-fold grid-search cross-validation within the training set. On the common test set (n = 840), CatBoost, XGBoost, and the multilayer perceptron each achieved an overall accuracy of 95.95% (Cohen’s κ = 0.947), followed by Gradient Tree Boosting (95.83%); McNemar tests with Holm correction detected no significant differences among these four models. Spatial block cross-validation reduced overall accuracy by 0.3–2.7 percentage points, and CatBoost retained the highest spatially blocked accuracy (95.51% with 10 km blocks). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified slope, SATVI, NDWI, and the blue band as the dominant contributors to CatBoost forest predictions. The leading maps estimated 859,057–870,663 ha of forest. CatBoost captured 90.9% of the Hansen forest extent (≥30% canopy cover) but mapped a much larger forest area; blind interpretation of stratified samples showed that 90.5% of the CatBoost-only forest was woody vegetation, mainly open woodland and matorral. These findings show that boosting ensembles combined with a compact, non-redundant predictor set provide accurate and spatially robust forest-cover maps and that differences from global products largely reflect forest definitions.

title: Non-Negative Latent Factorization Autoencoder for Interpretable Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection
summary: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (HAD) requires effective background modeling while limiting the reconstruction of rare anomalous spectra. Conventional non-negative matrix factorization provides an interpretable endmember–abundance representation but offers limited flexibility for estimating background representations under complex spectral variability, whereas reconstruction-oriented autoencoders provide flexible nonlinear inference but often lack an explicit mixing-model structure. To bridge these two paradigms, we propose a Non-negative Latent Factorization Autoencoder (NLFA) for anomaly-oriented background modeling. NLFA employs a nonlinear encoder to estimate simplex-constrained abundance-like latent coefficients and a linear mixing model (LMM)-consistent linear decoder to represent the dominant background through endmember-like spectral bases. A column-sparse residual is jointly optimized with the latent factorization so that spectral components insufficiently explained by the learned background are retained for anomaly detection, while local spatial smoothness and endmember-diversity constraints regularize the background representation. Experiments on eight benchmark hyperspectral datasets show that NLFA achieves competitive detection performance.

title: Forest Digital Terrain Model from Copernicus GLO-30 DEM and GEDI L2A Using an Explainable Boosting Machine
summary: Accurate ground elevation beneath forest canopies is important for terrain and forest-structure analysis, yet satellite-based elevation data can be affected by canopy and terrain conditions, while spaceborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) provides ground elevations only at discrete locations. Here, the elevation offset between the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM (CopDEM) and Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) L2A ground elevation was estimated using an Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) with topographic, canopy-structure, and CopDEM-uncertainty predictors to generate continuous forest digital terrain models (DTMs) for two regions in the Republic of Korea. Validation against independent airborne LiDAR data showed root mean square errors (RMSEs) of the proposed DTM of 4.10 m in the central-western region and 3.67 m in the eastern region. In the EBM, the CopDEM height error mask (HEM), canopy cover, and aspect contributed most to the estimated offset, and the magnitude and direction of their contributions varied across canopy–terrain conditions and between regions. Residual bias increased with canopy height and became more negative on steep slopes, where RMSE also increased. These results show that the proposed approach can generate continuous forest DTMs while quantifying the contributions of the main predictors to the offset, their variation across environmental conditions, and the conditions under which residual errors increase.

title: Machine Learning Reveals Physiologically Relevant Spectral Domains for Citrus Huanglongbing Detection
summary: Huanglongbing (HLB) is the most destructive disease affecting citrus production worldwide, causing severe yield losses and tree decline. Hyperspectral proximal sensing provides detailed information on leaf reflectance; however, its effectiveness for reliable HLB detection depends on the identification of consistent and discriminative spectral patterns. In this study, hyperspectral reflectance data (400–2450 nm) were combined with supervised machine learning algorithms to distinguish HLB-positive and HLB-negative citrus samples at two complementary scales: (i) leaf-level classification using individual spectral signatures and (ii) plant-level classification based on aggregated spectral responses. Model performance was evaluated under a leave-one-field-out validation framework designed to minimize spatial dependence between training and testing data. Results demonstrated consistently high classification performance, with Logistic Regression achieving accuracies above 0.94 at the leaf level and up to 1.00 at the plant level in several configurations. Dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) preserved most of the discriminative information, although with a slight reduction in recall under certain FIELD combinations. In contrast, Class balancing produced no observed improvement, whereas hyperparameter optimization showed limited and configuration-dependent effects in classification performance. Spectral coefficient analysis revealed that the most relevant wavelengths are concentrated in the visible (400–700 nm), red-edge (700–750 nm), near-infrared (750–1300 nm), and shortwave infrared (1500–2500 nm) regions, reflecting physiological alterations associated with pigment degradation, mesophyll disruption, and changes in water and biochemical composition. Overall, hyperspectral reflectance combined with parsimonious machine learning models enabled consistent discrimination of HLB-positive and HLB-negative samples within the evaluated orchard under validation designed to reduce spatial dependence, particularly at the plant scale.

title: A Second-Order Spatial Guided Sampling Method for Outlier Removal in UAV Remote Sensing Image Registration
summary: Image registration is fundamental to UAV remote sensing data processing, but repetitive textures, viewpoint and scale variations, terrain relief, and local deformation can introduce numerous outliers into tentative correspondences. The existing random-sampling and spatial-consistency methods commonly rely on pointwise confidence or isolated pairwise relations and therefore cannot reliably determine whether a locally compatible relation receives stable group-level structural support. To address this limitation, we propose SPGSC++, a second-order spatial guided sampling method for outlier removal. SPGSC++ first uses PCA to reduce the dimensionality of tentative correspondences, thereby reducing the computational burden of subsequent spatial relation construction. It then derives second-order structural quality from the common-neighbor support of directly compatible edges and uses this quality for initial data subset selection and residual-informed data subset refinement to generate and optimize a homography. Comparative experiments show that, on the five datasets CIAP, SUIRD, UAV, ZHANGZHOU, and PAN, the proposed method achieves mean Precision, Recall, F-Score, Runtime, and mean reprojection error values of 0.9627, 0.9797, 0.9702, 0.3724 s, and 1.6454, respectively. Relative to the original SPGSC, SPGSC++ increases the mean F-Score by 0.0391 and reduces Runtime and mean reprojection error by 32.39% and 58.12%, respectively. Overall, the innovation of SPGSC++ lies in using second-order common-neighbor structural quality to guide initial subset selection and residual-informed refinement for robust estimation in UAV remote sensing image registration.

title: MoEMamba: Mixture-of-Scale-And-Attention-Experts Mamba Network for Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: The Mamba network has recently emerged as a powerful architecture for remote sensing change detection (RSCD). Notably, the fusion of multi-scale features and heterogeneous attention mechanisms has proven effective in enhancing the performance of Mamba network. However, existing methods fail to quantitatively evaluate the actual contribution weights of different components during feature fusion, thereby limiting the interpretability of their improvements. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel mixture-of-scale-and-attention-experts Mamba Network (MoEMamba) for the RSCD task, which has the following innovations and contributions: (1) a Siamese Mamba architecture is employed to extract features from bi-temporal images; (2) a mixture-of-scale-experts module is designed to enhance the generalization ability across multi-scale objects, which quantitatively evaluates the contribution of multiple scale-specific experts; and (3) a mixture-of-attention-experts module is proposed to improve the accuracy, which adaptively fuses complementary responses of heterogeneous attention mechanisms based on the learned weights. Extensive experiments on the WHU-CD and LEVIR-CD datasets demonstrate that MoEMamba outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, it achieves F1 scores of 94.20% and 92.62%, and IoU values of 89.04% and 86.25%, respectively.
