Importantly, this study provides valuable insights into the interpretability of multi-scale feature fusion and heterogeneous attention fusion for RSCD research.

title: A Controlled Intercomparison of Altimeter Wet Tropospheric Correction Retrieval Algorithms Using Sentinel-6MF Observations
summary: A key correction in altimetry measurements is the wet tropospheric correction (WTC), which accounts for the delay on the measured range predominantly caused by water vapor in the troposphere. The WTC is currently one of the main sources of error affecting the altimeter range over ocean surfaces, with direct impact on estimates of sea surface height and the global mean sea level. Most current altimetry missions rely on onboard passive microwave radiometers that measure the brightness temperature at key frequencies for the spatio-temporal collocated estimation of the WTC. For such missions, the current operational algorithms for the estimation of the WTC can be placed in two categories: those using a neural network and those using a log-linear equation dependent on classes of WTC and windspeed. These two methodologies both follow a semi-empirical approach, but differ significantly in the inputs used, the training databases on which they are developed, and the mathematical approach itself. The objective of this study is to conduct a comprehensive comparison between these two algorithms, focusing solely on the mathematical aspect, in order to determine if the differences in the approaches of the two algorithms have a significant effect on the resulting WTC products, their performance and their limitations. To ensure the identical conditions required to achieve this, we develop the two algorithms so that they take the same inputs, have the same training database, and then we apply them to identical simulated and observed datasets to determine their performance. We use the three-frequency configuration (18.7 GHz−23.8 GHz−34 GHz) of the Advanced Microwave Radiometer for Climate (AMR-C) on Copernicus Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich (Sentinel-6MF), and radiative transfer modelling using the Radiative Transfer for TOVS (RTTOV), to create a simulated database that will serve for both development of the algorithms and performance evaluation. Both algorithms are then applied to the same observations from Copernicus Sentinel-6MF to characterise their observational performance in comparison to both model and operational products, as well as to each other. We find that, despite the significant differences in the two methodologies, when the algorithms are developed and applied to the same databases, they deliver very similar performances both on simulated and observed datasets and face similar limitations. In addition, for both algorithms we find performances similar to or slightly better than that of the operational WTC product for Copernicus Sentinel-6MF.

title: A Spatio-Temporal Fusion Method for Mine Subsidence Based on Decoupling the Basic Deformation Field from Residuals Using InSAR-GNSS
summary: Ground surface subsidence resulting from underground mining is characterized by significant spatial deformation gradients and nonlinear temporal deformation. A single monitoring technique is insufficient to simultaneously achieve extensive spatial coverage and high temporal continuity. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides high spatial resolution but is limited by sparse temporal sampling, whereas the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) offers dense temporal sampling but with restricted spatial coverage. To address these limitations, this study introduces a spatio-temporal fusion method combining InSAR and GNSS, based on baseline deformation field–residual decoupling (BR-STKF), specifically applied to the Banji Coal Mine in the Huainan Mining Area, Anhui Province. Sentinel-1 SBAS-InSAR is employed to derive Line-Of-Sight (LOS) deformation time series, while three-dimensional GNSS displacements are projected onto the LOS direction. A daily scale baseline deformation field is constructed using pixel-wise Kalman filtering and Rauch–Tung–Striebel (RTS) smoothing. Subsequently, residual signals between the InSAR/GNSS observations and the baseline field are estimated utilizing a correlation-anchored multiscale spatial basis and an information-form Kalman filter. Helmert variance component estimation is introduced to adaptively adjust the weights of InSAR and GNSS observations. To demonstrate the reliability of the proposed framework, a quantitative validation was conducted. The experimental results yielded root mean square error (RMSE) values of 6.37 mm for strict spatial leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) and 2.84 mm for retrospective reconstruction with missing InSAR phases. These results are competitive and comparable to leading benchmarks such as the Spatio-Temporal Kalman Filter (STKF), while achieving lower mean RMSEs than baseline methods such as Spatio-Temporal Random Effects (STREs), Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Random Effects (eSTREs), Improved Spatio-Temporal Random Effects (ISTREs), Multi-resolution Orthogonal Polynomial Basis (MOP), and ST-Kriging. However, the statistical stability of differences among models requires further verification with additional independent data. The findings suggest that the baseline deformation field–residual decoupling strategy effectively integrates the spatial coverage of InSAR with daily GNSS observations, offering a viable framework for daily scale line-of-sight (LOS) deformation reconstruction in mining areas.

title: Contrasting Vegetation Productivity Responses to Four Compound Temperature and Soil Moisture Extremes Across China
summary: Compound temperature and soil moisture extremes threaten terrestrial carbon uptake, but their contrasting ecological impacts remain poorly understood. We assessed dry–hot (DH), wet–hot (WH), dry–cold (DC), and wet–cold (WC) events across China from 2001 to 2025. The analyses combined daily air temperature, root-zone soil moisture, and MODIS-derived gross primary productivity (GPP). We quantified event occurrence, negative-response probability, cumulative GPP loss, and recovery time, and examined environmental predictors using explainable machine learning. WC events were most frequent, whereas DH events lasted longest. WH frequency increased over the study period, while DC frequency declined. DH and DC produced negative GPP responses in 63.5% and 67.1% of classifiable events, respectively. Among negative-response events, DH had the largest national mean cumulative event-period GPP loss below the −0.5 SD threshold (2.85 g C m−2) and the longest conditional recovery time (3.17 days). WC losses exceeded DC losses despite a lower negative-response probability. Losses varied with elevation, season, and event severity. Vapor pressure deficit dominated predictions of DH negative responses and losses, whereas other event types showed greater contributions from radiation, precipitation, and soil texture. These findings highlight the need to distinguish event occurrence, response probability, productivity loss, and recovery when assessing ecological risks from compound extremes.

title: Improved Forest Parameter Estimation Using Registered Airborne–Terrestrial Point Clouds via a Novel Adaptive Clustering and Vertical Layering Method
summary: Diameter at breast height (DBH) and tree height are core parameters for forest monitoring. LiDAR enables rapid high-precision point cloud acquisition, yet single-platform data have limitations: airborne laser scanning (ALS) cannot capture sub-canopy structure, while terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) cannot fully acquire canopy information. Based on 92 plots in Guangxi, this study proposes a weighted point-to-normal iterative closest point (WPN-ICP) registration algorithm for high-precision fusion of ALS and TLS point clouds, with comparisons to trimmed iterative closest point (TrICP) and iterative closest point (ICP). An adaptive density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) algorithm was developed for diameter at breast height (DBH) estimation, and a DBH cluster-based vertical layering method (DCVL-THE) for tree height estimation. Three segmentation-based methods—canopy height model (CHM), region growing (RG), and comparative shortest path (CSP)—were selected for comparison. WPN-ICP achieved a mean MAE of 0.0359 m, with reductions of 85.87%, 69.03%, and 73.00% compared with coarse registration, TrICP, and ICP. Using the fused point cloud, DBH estimation achieved an RMSE of 0.6326 cm with an RRMSE of 5.18%, and tree height estimation achieved an RMSE of 0.7160 m with an RRMSE of 6.58%. Compared with the suboptimal CSP method, the RMSE and RRMSE for DBH were reduced by 41.79% and 41.68%, and for tree height by 25.66% and 25.68%. This method does not require full individual-tree or crown segmentation, thereby avoiding the error propagation associated with such segmentation and enabling accurate stand-scale estimation.

title: ECSA-UNet: End-to-End Compressive Spatial-Spectral Attention UNet for Hyperspectral Image Classification
summary: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is a fundamental remote sensing task, but the high-dimensional nature of HSI data poses challenges for acquisition, storage, transmission, and processing. To mitigate these issues, researchers have developed compressive classification methods based on the coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI) system, enabling direct classification in the compressed domain without reconstructing the full hyperspectral cube. However, existing methods often fail to fully leverage spatial-spectral correlations, suffer from limited multi-scale feature extraction, and are constrained by fixed receptive fields and degradation caused by compression. To overcome these limitations, we propose ECSA-UNet, an end-to-end framework that directly classifies compressive spectral measurements from CASSI. The model introduces a spatial-spectral decoupling module and refines the U-Net architecture with global–local feature extraction, Spatial-Spectral Attention, a Multi-Scale Enhancement Pyramid and Cross-Stage Connections, enabling dynamic receptive fields, improved long-range dependency modeling, and robust local–global feature fusion. Moreover, the CASSI coded aperture is parameterized as a trainable component, allowing for joint optimization of coding and classification within an end-to-end learning paradigm. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks show ECSA-UNet achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, and ablations confirm each module’s contribution. In addition, it maintains an effective trade-off between parameter overhead and computational efficiency, offering a viable solution for latency-sensitive hyperspectral remote sensing tasks.

title: A Scanline Keypoint Constraint-Based Method for Correcting Scale-like Errors in UAV-ALB
summary: To address scale-like errors in local point clouds caused by pitch angle errors in unmanned aerial vehicle-borne LiDAR bathymetry (UAV-ALB) systems, this study proposes a correction method based on scanline keypoint constraints. First, the point cloud is traversed using scanline information to extract geometric keypoint features from each scanline. Next, a scale-like error correction model is constructed based on the distance differences between keypoints at the start and end of overlapping scanlines, and the pitch angle correction value is estimated using a forward–backward fusion approach. The estimated correction is then applied to the attitude data, and the point cloud is reprocessed. This procedure is iterated until the convergence criterion is satisfied. Experimental results show that, after correction, the horizontal root mean square errors (RMSE) of the two datasets decrease from 0.217 and 0.283 m to 0.025 and 0.030 m, respectively, while the elevation RMSE values decrease from 0.227 and 0.241 m to 0.006 and 0.004 m, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively mitigates scale-like errors in UAV-ALB point clouds and substantially improves their geometric consistency and elevation accuracy.

title: Adaptive Stratified Screening and Weakly Supervised UNet with Sparse ALS Refinement for Forest Canopy Height Mapping
summary: Forest canopy height is a key parameter for estimating forest biomass and carbon stocks, as well as a fundamental indicator for assessing forest ecosystem health. Although existing 10 m resolution global canopy height products are free and open-source, they suffer from substantial systematic errors due to the inherent biases of spaceborne LiDAR and the nonlinear relationship between optical imagery and canopy height, making them insufficiently accurate as direct training labels for deep learning. This study proposes a complete framework of “adaptive stratified screening, followed by weakly supervised UNet training and minimal ALS post-processing refinement.” First, using the 12 spectral bands of Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, the OOB distance is calculated via weighted random forest as an anomaly metric. Through systematic comparison of three anomaly metrics (Cook’s distance, OOB distance, and standardized residuals) and five retention ratios (30–50%), the OOB distance at 40% retention is identified as optimal. An adaptive retention strategy based on tree height stratification is then implemented: for low-tree areas (<20 m), 40% of low-anomaly samples are uniformly retained; for tall-tree areas (≥20 m), the retention ratio is dynamically adjusted according to the proportion of tall-tree pixels (95% when tall-tree proportion < 10%, 70% when 10–30%, and 50% when ≥30%). The screened high-confidence Lang data are then used as supervisory signals to train a UNet model for predicting canopy height across the entire region, producing an initial canopy height map (MAE = 6.97 m, Bias = +4.21 m). Finally, using only a minimal amount of airborne LiDAR data (down to 0.1% area proportion), with a 14-dimensional input comprising the initial predicted height, screening mask values, and the 12 spectral bands of Sentinel-2, a multilayer perceptron is independently trained for each region to perform post-processing refinement of the initial predictions. Experiments based on 68 independent regions from the Open-Canopy dataset, with a strict regional split (34 validation/34 test), show that post-processing refinement reduces the test set MAE from 6.97 m (ASS) to 3.29 m (0.1% ALS, a 52.8% improvement, 58.1% improvement over the original Lang product), Bias from +4.21 m to −0.13 m, and RMSE from 8.95 m to 4.72 m. Even when the ALS proportion is reduced to 0.01%, the MAE remains 3.57 m (a 48.8% improvement). Statistical significance testing (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, n = 34) indicates that ASS+MLP(0.1%) significantly outperforms ASS (p < 0.00001). This study provides an effective technical pathway for regional refinement of global canopy height products.

title: Consistency of HY-2B/C/D Altimeter Sea State Products in Chinese Coastal Seas: Wave Height, Wind Speed, and Parameter-Dependent Inter-Satellite Bias
summary: The HY-2B/C/D constellation delivers routine altimeter significant wave height (SWH) and sea-surface wind speed over the Chinese coastal seas through four product streams (GDR, IDR, ODR, and SDR), yet whether the three satellites are mutually consistent, and whether that consistency is the same for both parameters, has not been established. We assess three years (2023–2025) of 1 Hz Ku-band retrievals against 30 quality-controlled coastal buoys, using a deduplicated matchup database, a common-buoy and common-period protocol with bootstrap confidence intervals, and triple collocation against ERA5. Within each satellite, the product streams are consistent for both parameters: the reprocessed GDR shifts the operational SWH by a sea-state-independent −0.157 m and the wind streams coincide to rounding. Across satellites, consistency is parameter-dependent. For SWH, the biases on common buoys span 0.18 m; HY-2B has the lowest random error, significantly lower than HY-2D, and HY-2C cannot be separated from either in random error. For wind speed, HY-2C reads about 1 m s−1 low in all four Chinese seas and in every wind band once the bands are defined by an independent reference, so that most of the offset is removable by a constant. The near-shore degradation of SWH inside 50 km largely reflects the sub-0.5 m sea states that dominate the near-shore buoys, and wind speed shows no comparable coastal signal. We translate these findings into applicability bounds and a parameter-aware recipe for merging the constellation.

title: TP-YOLO: Thermal-Prior-Enhanced Photovoltaic Anomaly Detection in UAV Thermal Infrared Imagery
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) thermal infrared remote sensing can rapidly acquire thermal-response information for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) arrays. Nevertheless, local thermal anomalies occupy small regions within aerial images; their features tend to degrade during successive down-sampling. Moreover, model deployment on edge devices is constrained by limited computational and memory resources. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TP-YOLO, a photovoltaic anomaly-detection approach, and implements it on the Zynq-7020 hardware platform. First, a three-channel thermal-prior input consisting of luminance distribution, local luminance difference, and a luminance gradient is constructed from pseudo-color infrared images, and explicitly characterizes thermal anomalies without requiring absolute-temperature measurements. Next, the detection scales of YOLOv11n are adjusted to P2/P3/P4. Modules including A-C3k2, Conv + Add, and TLCB are adopted to optimize feature extraction and multi-scale fusion, preserving local anomaly features while restraining model complexity. On the hardware side, a PS/PL co-processing architecture is employed. A dedicated convolution IP, ADD IP, and Window IP are designed for convolution, element-wise fusion, and local-window operations, respectively. INT8 quantization and ping-pong buffering are further utilized to realize network deployment. On the PV HSD test set, TP-YOLO achieves an mAP@0.5 of 77.5% and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 33.7%, with 1.91 M parameters and 6.2 GFLOPs computational cost. In cross-dataset evaluation on the Drone Dataset without fine-tuning, the mAP@0.5 reaches 64.4%. After deploying the INT8 quantized model onto Zynq-7020, the implemented system yields an mAP@0.5 of 76.8%, achieving single-frame inference latency of 162 ms and throughput of 6.17 FPS at 150 MHz, with a power consumption of 3.4 W.

title: Cross-Configuration 4D DAS-VSP Monitoring for Long-Term CO2 Storage
summary: Safe and reliable carbon capture and storage (CCS) requires long-term monitoring to verify secure CO2 containment. Distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profiling (DAS-VSP) provides a practical approach for subsurface monitoring due to its permanent installation, dense spatial sampling, and reduced operational costs. However, monitoring programs spanning decades may require hardware upgrades, including interrogator replacements and changes to fibre-optic cable configurations, affecting time-lapse repeatability and interpretability. This field case study evaluates whether the CO2-induced 4D DAS-VSP response remains interpretable across a combined change in interrogator, fibre type and optical path, whose individual contributions cannot be isolated. The assessment uses data from the CO2CRC Otway Project Stage 4, where approximately 10 kilotons of CO2-rich reservoir gas were injected into a saline aquifer at approximately 1500 m depth. Baseline and monitor surveys using different DAS configurations are compared at two monitoring wells, with a same-configuration case as a repeatability benchmark. An established 4D DAS-VSP processing workflow, supplemented by system-specific noise attenuation, is applied to mitigate configuration-dependent differences. The results show that, despite higher non-repeatability, the principal CO2-related time-lapse anomaly remains spatially localised and distinguishable, indicating that the DAS-VSP response can remain interpretable across a combined configuration change under favourable acquisition and signal-quality conditions.

title: Long-Term Wetland Resilience Monitoring Using Landsat Time Series and a LandTrendr–GWRF Framework in Northeast China
summary: Long-term monitoring of wetland degradation, recovery, and spatial resilience requires methods that can jointly exploit multi-temporal remote sensing observations and spatially heterogeneous environmental information. This study develops an intelligent remote sensing framework for monitoring the disturbance–recovery dynamics and spatial resilience of typical wetland landscapes in Northeast China by coupling Landsat-based Detection of Trends in Disturbance and Recovery (LandTrendr) with geographically weighted random forest (GWRF). Annual wetland landscape state sequences for 2000–2022 are constructed from multi-temporal Landsat observations and associated geospatial variables. LandTrendr time-series segmentation is used to identify disturbance timing, disturbance magnitude, recovery rate, and recovery duration, thereby converting long-term wetland change trajectories into quantitative indicators of degradation and recovery. At the GIS grid scale, remotely sensed vegetation and wetness indicators are integrated with wetland patch structure, hydrological conditions, topography, land-cover change, and anthropogenic pressure. GWRF then models local nonlinear relationships under spatial-distance weighting to generate a spatially explicit wetland resilience index and reveal geographically varying dominant controls. The LandTrendr–GWRF model achieved an R2 of 0.872, an RMSE of 0.057, and an MAE of 0.039, outperforming RF, GWR, XGBoost, and standalone GWRF benchmarks. The mean wetland resilience index was 0.641, with low-, medium-, and high-resilience areas accounting for 27.86%, 44.37%, and 27.77% of the study area, respectively. Significant spatial clustering was detected (Moran’s I = 0.421, Z = 6.92, p = 0.001). Hydrological regulation, landscape connectivity, fragmentation constraint, and anthropogenic disturbance pressure emerged as the four dominant spatial response types. High-resilience cells formed contiguous clusters where hydrological recharge and landscape connectivity were strong, while low-resilience cells clustered where fragmentation and construction pressure were concentrated. Disturbance magnitude and recovery duration differed markedly among the four response types, with connectivity-dominated cells returning to the pre-disturbance state within 4.4 years and anthropogenic pressure-dominated cells requiring 11.7 years. The proposed framework extends wetland remote sensing from static condition mapping toward process-oriented monitoring of degradation, recovery, connectivity, and resilience, providing a practical approach for long-term wetland restoration assessment and spatial management.

title: Aboveground Biomass Estimation in Pure Calabrian Pine Stands of Southern Türkiye Using Multi-Seasonal Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Variables: A Multi-Seasonal Comparison
summary: Aboveground biomass (AGB) is considered a key variable in surveilling the sustainability of forest management and the carbon cycle. This study examined the effects of image acquisition season and topographic variables on the performance of AGB estimates using Sentinel-2 imagery from three seasons. The study was conducted in 224 sample plots in pure Calabrian pine (Pinus brutia) stands in southern Türkiye. Random forest models were trained on 26 datasets derived from rainy, arid, and semi-arid season imagery, including single-season, two-season, and three-season combinations with and without topographic variables. Models trained using satellite images from rainy and semi-arid seasons performed better than models trained using data from the more arid season. All two-season combinations outperformed the corresponding single-season models, but none reached the accuracy of the three-season model. Including topographic variables reduced RMSE for every season and season combination. The best results were obtained using all three seasons together with topographic variables (R2 = 0.74, RMSE = 13.97 Mg ha−1), and removing topography from this model increased RMSE to 15.69 Mg ha−1. According to the SHAP analysis, elevation was the second-most influential predictor after Aug_SAVI (mean SHAP value = 1.65 Mg ha−1) and the only topographic variable that notably contributed to predictive performance. These findings indicate that, for the pure Calabrian pine stands and conditions examined in this study, combining multi-seasonal Sentinel-2 imagery with topographic variables improves AGB estimation accuracy compared with single-season models and spectral data alone.

title: A Machine Learning Approach for XCH4 Retrieval over China Based on TROPOMI Spectral Features
summary: Methane is a major greenhouse gas that plays a critical role in climate change. Accurate monitoring of methane at the regional scale is essential for understanding its spatiotemporal dynamics and underlying processes. Here, a machine learning-based framework is developed to retrieve column-averaged methane (XCH4) by integrating shortwave infrared spectral information from TROPOMI. Spectral channels are first analyzed through machine learning-based feature importance analysis, and normalized spectral features are subsequently constructed. These features are then combined with auxiliary variables, including meteorological conditions, observation geometry, and surface environmental factors, to develop an XCH4 retrieval model. The GOSAT L2 XCH4 product is introduced as a high-accuracy reference observation for correcting the retrieved XCH4 results, and independent validation is conducted using observations from the TCCON site. Among the evaluated models, XGBoost demonstrates the best performance, achieving an R2 of 0.91 and an RMSE of 9.28 ppb under five-fold cross-validation. The model also maintains relatively better predictive performance compared with other models under both temporal and spatial extrapolation scenarios. Compared with the TROPOMI L2 product, the retrieved XCH4 shows improved agreement with TCCON observations, with a higher correlation (R = 0.84) and reduced errors. Based on this approach, a daily, spatially continuous XCH4 dataset over China for 2021 is generated. Analysis of the retrieved dataset reveals pronounced spatiotemporal patterns, characterized by higher XCH4 concentrations in eastern China and lower values in the western regions, as well as a distinct seasonal cycle.

title: Largely Automated Regional Screening of Candidate Active-Slope Units Integrating InSAR and Topographic Constraints
summary: Landslides are among the most serious geohazards worldwide, and accurately identifying their locations is a prerequisite for effective risk prevention and mitigation. However, regional-scale screening of candidate active-slope units from InSAR observations is still hindered by subjective manual interpretation, inconsistent deformation-rate thresholds, and insufficient topographic constraints. To address these limitations, this study proposes a largely automated terrain-constrained framework for candidate active-slope screening by integrating InSAR observations, slope units, and screening based on slope-unit bootstrap intervals and a regional two-standard-deviation background envelope. First, surface deformation rates are derived from InSAR measurements and post-processed to reduce the influence of identifiable artifacts before slope-unit analysis. Then, a clustering-based method is introduced to delineate topographically constrained slope units in alpine canyon regions, whose visual terrain correspondence is examined qualitatively using terrain information and optical imagery. Next, rather than applying a fixed site-specific deformation-rate cutoff in mm/yr, data-dependent bootstrap confidence-interval comparisons are used to determine whether the deformation interval of each slope unit extends beyond the regional deformation-background interval, thereby enabling rule-based screening of candidate active-slope units. This confidence-interval screening rule provides a quantitative criterion for regional screening but requires further calibration across additional geomorphic and deformation settings. Finally, the proposed method is applied to two landslide-prone regions in western China, located in sections of the Upper Yellow River and Upper Jinsha River, where final inventories containing 92 and 25 candidate active-slope units are produced, respectively. These polygons are geomorphologically constrained candidate active-slope units produced for regional screening and should not be interpreted as the exact boundaries of individual landslides. Inventory-based spatial comparison and targeted optical inspection were reported as complementary evidence streams rather than as independent validation of contemporaneous slope activity. These results document implementation in two related alpine river-valley settings in western China and indicate the framework’s potential as a quantitatively defined, topographically constrained approach for largely automated regional screening of candidate active-slope units in comparable settings. These two applications do not establish broad applicability across substantially different environments.

title: Task-Oriented Evaluation of Eight Cropland Maps for Agricultural Monitoring in China
summary: Differences in cropland definitions, spatial resolution, and mapping strategies complicate product selection. We harmonized and evaluated eight 2020 cropland and land-cover products across mainland China using hierarchically labeled probability samples. Fixed map predictions enabled comparisons across common task-specific and product-definition-matched reference labels. Evaluation covered spatial agreement, design-weighted classification accuracy, design-based area bias, cropland-type responses, and cross-scale performance. Only 26.8% of pixels in the cropland union were classified as cropland by all products. Within the consensus-cropland evaluation domain, CropLayer achieved the highest overall accuracy (0.961) and F1 score (0.844). CCropLand30 led 30 m products in F1, whereas the Esri land-cover product (ESRI-LC) had national area bias closest to zero (−2.26%). Most 30 m products showed commission-dominated errors and positive area bias. Product responses varied across cropland types, and reference labels altered performance estimates. Switching from unified-agriculture to product-definition-matched labels reduced ESRI-LC’s F1 from 0.765 to 0.682 and shifted area bias from −8.08% to +14.88%. Spatial aggregation reduced F1 for some fine-resolution products without consistently changing local cropland-proportion error. These results show that classification accuracy and area bias yield different rankings, supporting product selection according to application, cropland definition, landscape context, evaluation metric, and spatial support.

title: Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction for Blind Hyperspectral Image Unmixing
summary: Recent blind hyperspectral image unmixing methods have achieved effective spectral–spatial representation, yet the reliability of estimated abundances remains difficult to assess because errors in jointly estimated endmembers and abundances can compensate for each other. To address this issue, we propose Residual Diagnosis-Guided Abundance Correction (RDAC), a post-correction framework that preserves the initial abundance estimate as an anchor and characterizes its mismatch using structured reconstruction residuals. Abundance candidates are then combined with structured residual information, while only 1% reference abundances are used to learn the correction. RDAC was evaluated on the Jasper Ridge, Samson, and Urban datasets. With UNMamba as the primary blind-unmixing backbone, RDAC achieved A-RMSEs of 0.0229, 0.0175, and 0.0359, reducing the initial errors by 55.05%, 70.80%, and 59.63%, respectively. It also achieved the lowest mean A-RMSE among the compared methods on Jasper Ridge and Samson while remaining competitive on Urban. Further experiments showed that reconstruction error alone does not reliably indicate abundance accuracy. When applied to NMF, RDAC reduced A-RMSE by 80.45%, 89.25%, and 77.61% on the three datasets. The results indicate that structured residual diagnosis can support abundance correction under limited supervision, and the NMF experiment shows that the same correction framework can also be used with an alternative blind-unmixing backbone.

title: Insights into Intense Lightning Activity During the Lifetime of Super Typhoon Doksuri (2023)
summary: The characteristics and formation mechanisms of lightning activity during the lifetime of Super Typhoon Doksuri (2023) were investigated using ERA5 reanalysis data and observation data from the World-Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) and Himawari-8/9 satellite. The lightning activity exhibited pronounced intermittent outbreak behavior, and intense lightning flashes mainly occurred in the outer rainband region approximately 200–600 km from the typhoon center. The occurrence of intense lightning was mainly related to the development of deep convections which were characterized by a high CAPE index and low cloud-top brightness temperature. In the landfall stage, intense lightning outbreaks may have been further modulated by the orographic lifting from the underlying surface and island thermal effects. Strong updrafts within the typhoon provided favorable conditions for intracloud microphysical electrification processes. The formation of intense lightning was interpreted via the non-inductive charging mechanism and validated using E-WRF model simulations. During the first rapid-intensification episode, intense inner-core lightning preceded the typhoon intensity peak by 14–41 h; during the re-intensification episode, it occurred ~9 h after the typhoon peak. These insights into the intense lightning activity in Super Typhoon Doksuri (2023) contribute to improving typhoon forecasting and disaster warning in the Western Pacific.

title: Analysis of SMAP-R Polarimetric Information for Improved Sea Surface Wind Retrieval
summary: Spaceborne Global Navigation Satellite System reflectometry (GNSS-R) sea surface wind speed retrieval commonly relies on the normalized bistatic radar cross section (NBRCS), whose response depends on observation geometry, link conditions, signal quality, and sea state. Under low-wind, high-swell conditions, local wind speed alone cannot fully explain variations in reflected signals. We use SMAP-R hybrid compact polarimetric observations and ERA5 wind and wave data to assess whether polarimetric features improve sea surface wind speed retrieval. A dataset of 2,067,971 observations is divided by complete months into training, validation, calibration, and test sets. With total significant wave height included in every baseline, paired non-polarimetric and polarimetric configurations are evaluated on identical samples using a geophysical model function with minimum-variance fusion (GMF/MV), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and a fully connected network trained by back-propagation (BP-FCN). Adding the degree of polarization and normalized third Stokes component reduces the overall root mean square error (RMSE) by 7.83%, 5.49%, and 5.31%, respectively, with the polarimetric BP-FCN configuration achieving the lowest RMSE of 1.666 m s−1. Wind speed-stratified analysis shows that the relative error reduction from polarimetric information varies non-monotonically across wind speed intervals. Across all signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) intervals represented in this study, all three methods achieve positive polarimetric gains, with paired month-block bootstrap 95% intervals lying above zero, indicating benefits across different SNR conditions. Under low-wind, high-swell conditions, RMSE decreases by 10.58%, 11.26%, and 9.82%, respectively, exceeding the overall relative gains. Error decomposition indicates that these improvements mainly reflect reduced systematic overestimation. Comparisons against ASCAT scatterometer and NDBC buoy winds using all collocated samples also show positive polarimetric gains of 4.83–5.35% and 4.80–5.78%, respectively. These results demonstrate that polarimetric observations can further improve GNSS-R wind speed retrieval accuracy beyond the information already included in the baselines, with more pronounced gains under the low-wind, high-swell conditions sampled in this study, providing useful complementary information for sea surface wind speed retrieval under complex sea states.

title: A Multiscale Remote-Sensing Assessment of Root-Zone Soil Moisture, Evapotranspiration and Canopy Moisture Stress Across Uruguay During the 2020–2023 Drought
summary: Drought affects meteorological forcing, root-zone water availability and land-surface functioning at different spatial and temporal supports. We evaluated Uruguay’s 2020–2023 drought using an observational 2016–2024 panel of 1423 SMAP parent cells. Monthly SPEI-3, SPEI-6 and SPEI-12 represented short, intermediate and persistent climatic water-balance deficits. SMAP root-zone soil moisture (RZSM) was retained at 9 km support, whereas actual evapotranspiration (ETa) and the moisture stress index (MSI) were summarized from approximately 500 m pixels using annual MapBiomas fractions for grassland, cropland and silviculture within each parent cell. For each cell and 8-day composite position, responses were expressed relative to the corresponding 2016–2019 mean. An interval was classified as locally dry when its overlap-day-weighted SPEI-12 was below −1. During 2020–2023, RZSM responses ranged from −13.09% to −16.63% among dominant landscape domains. Fraction-weighted ETa responses were −8.69% for grassland, −6.75% for cropland and −7.39% for silviculture, while oriented MSI responses were −6.62%, −3.32% and −11.20%, respectively. At lag zero, monthly RZSM correlated the most strongly with SPEI-3 (r = 0.81), followed by SPEI-6 (r = 0.64) and SPEI-12 (r = 0.51). At native 8-day support, RZSM was positively aligned with ETa (r = 0.42–0.57) and the oriented MSI (r = 0.31–0.59), although prewhitening weakened some associations. Overall, the 2020–2023 drought was consistently expressed across meteorological, root-zone and land-surface indicators. The strong association between SPEI-3 and RZSM, together with consistent land-surface departures and product-dependent ETa variation among components, highlights the value of multiscale monitoring for characterizing drought intensity and ecosystem responses across Uruguay.

title: Remote Sensing Bathymetry of Nearshore Island Reefs via an Enhanced Dual-Stream Mixture Density Network
summary: High-resolution bathymetry is critical for nearshore reefs, navigation, and island engineering. This paper proposes an Enhanced Mixture Density Network (EMDN) using dual-stream feature disentanglement and mixed total variance regularization to improve both accuracy and reliability of satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB). Validated with ICESat-2 and Sentinel-2 data over island reefs in the South China Sea and Hawaii, EMDN achieves RMSEs of 1.20 m, 1.24 m, and 3.71 m at Ganquan, Guangjin, and West Molokai, with the lowest mean uncertainties (0.76 m, 0.75 m, 2.46 m). Comparisons with the evaluated baselines demonstrate improved bathymetric accuracy and lower CRPS values, together with sharper prediction intervals and competitive calibration, highlighting the potential of EMDN for nearshore reef bathymetric mapping.

title: Nonlinear Causal Evidence for Turbulence–Particle Growth Coupling: Insights from a Subtropical Freezing Rain Event
summary: Understanding and estimating the impact of atmospheric turbulence on the growth of precipitation particles in freezing weather can help improve the prediction of freezing rain precipitation. In this study, the turbulent kinetic energy dissipation rate (ε) during a freezing weather event was retrieved using the power spectral analysis method, based on observational data from a Ka-band millimeter-wave cloud radar, radiosondes, and ground automatic weather stations, and the influence of atmospheric turbulence on the growth of freezing rain precipitation particles was investigated using nonlinear causal methods such as transfer entropy (TE), convergent cross-mapping (CCM), the phase-randomized surrogate test, and partial CCM. Causality tests confirmed a significant bidirectional causal relationship between ε and Ze, with the information transfer from ε to Ze systematically dominating throughout the entire height range of precipitation particles. The bidirectional original ρ was far higher than the 99% quantile of the surrogate distribution, and the coupling was enhanced after removing the influence of temperature and humidity, indicating that it was independent of the thermodynamic covariant background. The causal intensity in the ice crystal growth zone above 6 km was approximately 3 times the average in the liquid zone, indicating that atmospheric turbulence is one of the key factors driving the growth of precipitation particles in freezing weather and that the effect is concentrated in the dominant layer of ice crystals. This finding provides a practical basis for improving the parameterization scheme and numerical prediction of the precipitation particle microphysical processes in freezing weather.

title: Hyperspectral Video Object Segmentation Based on Spectral–Spatial Interaction Enhancement and Adaptive Correlation Memory Selection
summary: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is an important imaging modality in the field of optical remote sensing, capable of simultaneously capturing spatial structures and continuous spectral responses related to material properties. Therefore, compared with conventional red-green-blue (RGB) images, it can provide richer representations for understanding dynamic scenes. However, most existing video object segmentation methods have been developed for RGB videos, while high-quality hyperspectral video datasets with frame-by-frame pixel-level annotations remain scarce. To address this gap, this study constructed a hyperspectral video object segmentation dataset, comprising hyperspectral videos and their corresponding three-channel false-color RGB videos derived from the same HSI data, with pixel-level annotations provided for each frame. The dataset contains three spectral subsets: visible (VIS), near-infrared (NIR), and red-edge near-infrared (RedNIR). Using this dataset, we developed SSAM-SAM2, a hyperspectral video object segmentation network built on Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2). The network includes a spectral–spatial interaction enhancement (SSIE) module designed to identify informative spectral bands, suppress interference from redundant and noisy spectral channels, and integrate hyperspectral cues with the spatial-structure features of the corresponding false-color RGB images. In addition, the network introduces an Adaptive Correlation Memory Selection (ACMS) module that regulates memory sampling and selection according to variations in target state and inter-frame feature correlation. This design reduces the influence of redundant or unreliable historical information and improves temporal memory reliability under target deformation, motion variations, and background interference. Extensive experiments show that SSAM-SAM2 outperforms the selected comparison methods on the VIS, NIR, and RedNIR subsets under the evaluated settings. These results demonstrate the value of the proposed dataset and indicate that spectral–spatial enhancement and temporal adaptive memory mechanisms contribute to improving hyperspectral video object segmentation performance.

title: CA-CFAR Soft Attention and Scatter-Aware Context Aggregation for Small Ship Detection in SAR Imagery
summary: Small ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is limited by feature loss at coarse strides, sea-clutter false alarms, and the sensitivity of small boxes to annotation offsets. We propose CaSA-DETR, a detector built on RT-DETRv2 with three components. CFAR-Attention is a CFAR-inspired local contrast normalisation that reweights the stride-8 and stride-16 features bypassing the Transformer encoder, using sliding-window background statistics. Scatter-Aware Context Aggregation (SACA) collects context at four dilation rates with parallel dilated depthwise-separable convolutions and branch-adaptive gating. Inner-GIoU computes the regression loss on the inner 49% of each box, intended to reduce the influence of boundary offsets on targets smaller than 32 by 32 pixels. On a benchmark of 44,217 training images (73,407 instances, all under 32 by 32 pixels), the full model with a ResNet-101-vd backbone at 1024 by 1024 input reaches an average precision (AP) of 60.75% and an F1 score of 90.10%, 3.96 AP above D-FINE at the same input size. A cross of backbone, input size and modules shows that most of the gain over the original RT-DETRv2 baseline comes from the higher input, and that the three modules add 1.0 to 1.4 AP at every backbone and input size tested. On 2244 ship-free images, the modules cut false alarms by about 30% at a confidence of 0.5, at a cost of 0.66% more parameters and 2.3% more floating-point operations (FLOPs). The three modules improve AP at low cost.

title: Research on the Development and Evolution of Multi-Source Fusion Navigation Technology
summary: In response to the application limitations of single-source navigation systems for their susceptibility to interference, insufficient positioning accuracy and limited scenario adaptability in complex environments, as well as the increasingly complex demands for high-precision, high-robustness, all-weather and all-scenario navigation services in fields such as the low-altitude economy, intelligent driving and specialized operations, multi-source fusion navigation technology is accelerating its evolution. This manuscript systematically reviews the development trajectory from reliance on a single navigation system to multi-source intelligent integrated navigation, dividing it into the following four evolutionary stages: single-system dominance, loose-tight coupling, deep integration and intelligent ubiquitous navigation stage. It focuses on a comparative analysis of the core characteristics, fusion modes, key technological breakthroughs, and practical limitations and bottlenecks of multi-source fusion technologies at each stage, with the aim of providing comprehensive reference for technological research and development, solution design and industrial implementation in related fields.

title: Reliability and Transferability of Marine Harmful Algal Bloom Detection Using Ocean-Color Satellite Observations: From Optical Signals to Trustworthy Products
summary: Satellite ocean-color remote sensing is used to detect harmful algal blooms (HABs), yet detection capability does not necessarily ensure reliable interpretation or transferable performance. If these limitations are overlooked when developing cross-regional or global automated HAB early-warning systems, biological claims may be overstated and regional changes in false-alarm or missed-detection rates may go unnoticed, potentially compromising warning reliability and related management decisions. We develop an evidence-constrained framework to evaluate both dimensions: reliability, defined by whether the observation–processing–inference chain supports the intended biological claim, and transferability, defined by whether task-relevant performance is retained under changes in time, region, sensor, or optical environment. A structured Web of Science search yielded 1212 unique records, from which 28 purposively prioritized full-text core studies underwent coding for validation design, cross-domain evidence, error, and uncertainty. The synthesis identifies an evidentiary gap between optical detection capability and biological claim specificity, while fixed-configuration cross-domain evidence was scarce and performance retention remained unquantified. Satellite observations can support bloom presence, optical phenotypes, and selected taxon-targeted applications, but specific claims require specific independent biological references. Reliability is constrained by reference and labeling practices, preprocessing, observation availability, and incomplete uncertainty characterization, while evidence for transferability is limited by insufficient source–target evaluation. We propose a framework linking claim–evidence alignment, independent validation, domain-shift assessment, and uncertainty reporting. Reliable and transferable HAB remote sensing should move beyond detection outputs toward evidence-supported, uncertainty-aware products for monitoring, early warning, and decision-making.

title: Correction: Qi et al. Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost. Remote Sens. 2026, 18, 3483
summary: No abstract available in OpenAlex.

title: Mask2Former–FGMBRM: A Feature-Guided Building Segmentation Framework for Automated 3D Urban Environment Generation from Satellite Imagery
summary: Building-footprint errors can propagate into geospatial assets generated from remote-sensing imagery. This study evaluated Mask2Former–FGMBRM, which applies feature-guided residual refinement to Mask2Former query-mask predictions and integrates extracted footprints with documented terrain data and geospatial processing for footprint-based urban asset generation. Six models were evaluated on 518 WHU held-out images using common final references and metric definitions while retaining model-specific pipelines. The tune-selected Mask2Former baseline and FGMBRM achieved AP values of 72.03% and 73.49%, respectively, a 1.47-percentage-point improvement. FGMBRM also achieved 89.01% binary IoU and 91.86% object F1, leading these measures and AP among the six configurations, whereas SegFormer had the highest boundary F1. Controlled ablations showed metric-dependent trade-offs, with simpler variants leading selected outcomes and no consistent advantage from query-conditioned guidance. The original INRIA comparison remained limited. In a separate query-capacity diagnostic, AP at common maxDets = 100 increased from 20.66% to 23.96%, while retaining more outputs increased recall and false positives. The results support footprint-based urban asset generation and visualization, with remaining dense-scene and geometric limitations.

title: Adverse-Weather Aerial Object Detection: From Degradation Mechanisms to Robustness Evidence
summary: Adverse weather degrades visibility, contrast, edges, and local target details in aerial imagery, while small object size, viewing geometry, and onboard constraints further amplify detection failures. This review examines how weather-induced degradation propagates from image formation to feature damage and detection errors, and evaluates the evidence supporting existing robustness claims. A structured search of studies published between 2015 and 2026 identified 174 candidate records, which were analysed in terms of degradation mechanisms, methodological pathways, datasets, evaluation protocols, training dependencies, and deployment conditions. Existing methods are grouped into input restoration, joint restoration–detection learning, degradation-aware representation, domain adaptation and generalisation, multimodal and temporal compensation, and lightweight deployment. The evidence shows that improved visual quality does not consistently translate into better detection performance, while many reported gains depend on paired data, target-domain access, external priors, additional sensors, or computational overhead. Current evidence remains strongly concentrated on haze, with limited validation for natural rain, snow, dust, compound weather, unseen-weather generalisation, uncertainty, and closed-loop flight. Future research should therefore prioritise realistic weather data, controlled evaluation, risk-aware assessment, and onboard validation.

title: An Investigation into Land Surface Temperature-Based Climate Indices
summary: Monitoring climate change is crucial to society, industry, and the environment to assess their vulnerability to such extreme temperature events and plan adaptation and mitigation strategies. Temperature-based climate indices, which are used for climate monitoring, are usually calculated using near-surface air temperature (NSAT) from weather stations. A limitation of NSAT is the inhomogeneity of station distribution across the globe, with some regions under-sampled. This study evaluates the potential of using land surface temperature (LST) retrieved via satellite to calculate temperature indices, because low Earth-orbiting satellites can observe almost all of the Earth. This work compares indices calculated from NSAT to those produced from LST, and the indices are aggregated by Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change AR6 regions. Results show that there is often moderate to high correlation between indices produced using NSAT and LST. In addition, it is found that monthly to seasonal changes in indices are similar for both variables, particularly in percentile-based indices. Threshold-based indices could not be calculated for some regions due to low data availability, and therefore this work also applies “relative” indices, where indices are normalised relative to the amount of data available. These generally also demonstrate high correlations between NSAT and LST and can better show when events, such as heatwaves, occur. Lastly, this work presents the potential of an LST-based temperature indices dataset and how uncertainties could be evaluated.

title: Estimation of Particulate Organic Carbon Concentration and Its Driving Factors in Lakes of the Yangtze–Huaihe Plain, China
summary: Inland lake ecosystems function as active nodes in the global carbon cycle, yet reliable basin-scale estimates of particulate organic carbon concentration (CPOC) remain scarce owing to the optical complexity of these environments. In this study, POC denotes the total particulate organic carbon pool, including organic matter from living and non-living particles. Here we present a semi-analytical retrieval scheme tailored to Sentinel-2 Multispectral Instrument (MSI) data and applied to 90 large eutrophic lakes (each >10 km2) within the Yangtze–Huaihe Plain (YHP) of eastern China. The scheme reconstructs the particulate absorption coefficient at 665 nm, ap(665), from reflectance measurements at 665, 705, and 740 nm, reducing the interference of colored dissolved organic matter (aCDOM) absorption and particulate backscattering (bb). When evaluated against 60 field observations in the predefined concentration-stratified holdout, the algorithm achieved MAE = 0.59 mg/L, RMSE = 0.73 mg/L, and MAPE = 46.89%—outperforming three widely cited benchmark algorithms—and showed preliminary transfer potential in the two estuarine datasets. MSI-derived CPOC maps from 2018 to 2024 revealed systematic east-to-west and center-to-periphery concentration gradients across the 90-lake assemblage, shaped by catchment nutrient delivery, basin hydrodynamics, and phytoplankton standing stock. Correlation and attribution analyses identified chlorophyll-a concentration (CChla), atmospheric pressure, and total phosphorus (CTP) as the three dominant environmental modulators of CPOC variability. The framework provides a field-calibrated approach for examining regional lake CPOC patterns. Its satellite application and ability to distinguish small concentration differences require further independent validation and uncertainty assessment.

title: Observations of Biomass Burning Smoke Transported from Southeast Asia Using a Multi-Wavelength Polarization Raman Lidar
summary: Biomass burning smoke (BBS) emitted from Southeast Asia can be transported through regional atmospheric circulation, exerting significant impacts on air quality and climate over southwestern China. However, continuous observations of the vertical structures and optical properties of transported BBS remain limited. This study used one year of continuous multi-wavelength polarization Raman lidar observations at Mengzi (23.37°N, 103.38°E) in Yunnan, China, to identify transboundary BBS transport events and characterize their optical properties. Eight transboundary BBS events originating from Southeast Asia were identified using a comprehensive data processing framework involving aerosol extinction coefficient, backscatter coefficient, lidar ratio, particle linear depolarization ratio (PDR), and Ångström exponent. The transported smoke layers were mainly distributed below 4 km, exhibiting significantly enhanced aerosol extinction coefficients of 0.22–0.32 km−1 (compared with 0.02–0.06 km−1 for background aerosols). The 532 nm lidar ratios of the smoke layers (49.0–68.3 sr) were higher than those of the background aerosols (31.6–39.0 sr). The particle linear depolarization ratios ranged from 0.050 to 0.097 at 532 nm and from 0.14 to 0.19 at 355 nm, revealing a pronounced wavelength dependence. These values indicate measurable particle depolarization but do not independently establish particle morphology or the degree of smoke aging. Hybrid Single-Particle Lagrangian Integrated Trajectory (HYSPLIT) backward trajectory analysis together with fire hotspot observations revealed that this smoke mainly originated from biomass burning regions over the Indochina Peninsula and was transported to Yunnan across northern Myanmar, Laos, and northern Vietnam. This study provides important observational evidence of transport pathways, vertical distribution, and optical properties of transboundary BBS aerosols transported from Southeast Asia to southwest China.

title: Improving Driver Attribution for Water-Level Variations in Qinghai Lake Through Hydrological Process-Period Analysis
summary: Daily water-level changes in alpine closed lakes integrate lake-surface exchange, cryosphere processes, basin storage, and runoff routing, yet fixed calendar seasons and synchronous predictors may mix contrasting hydrological states and misalign antecedent forcing. This study developed a Hydro-Lag framework for Qinghai Lake, China’s largest inland lake, during 2014–2023 to improve daily reconstruction and driver attribution through dynamic hydrological process periods and time-lag effects. Satellite altimetry, optical and thermal imagery, hydrometeorological reanalysis, lake ice, and runoff data were integrated with water-balance constraints. The frozen (T1) and ablation (T2) periods were identified from lake ice transitions and a positive degree-day (PDD) threshold estimated from ice thickness. Meanwhile, basin wetness, represented by the antecedent precipitation index (API), distinguished the wet (T3) and dry (T4) periods. Candidate lags from cross-correlation analysis were refined through repeated cross-validation and used in an ensemble of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and ExtraTrees; cross-fitted predictions were interpreted with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Alignments differed markedly: selected core variables in T1 aligned mainly at 10–12 days; T2 used 1–2 days runoff, soil-moisture, and evapotranspiration offsets together with a same-day 14-day M_snow accumulation; T3 runoff and soil moisture at 3–5 days and precipitation-related variables at 8–9 days; and T4 antecedent basin variables at 11–24 days. Against an independently tuned SeasonRAW baseline, Hydro-Lag increased test R2 from 0.551 to 0.793 and reduced RMSE from 14.26 to 8.51 mm d−1. OOF SHAP indicated period-dependent patterns in modeled predictor contributions: mixed contributions in T1, wetness–storage emphasis in T2–T3, and antecedent storage and thermo-evaporative contributions in T4. Conditional responses showed thresholds and sign reversals across thermal, wetness, and event-magnitude gradients. The framework provides a process-aware basis for assessing daily lake–basin interactions in data-sparse alpine closed basins.

title: Predicting Fuel Moisture Codes Across Mountainous Forests of British Columbia Using L-Band ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 Imagery
summary: Fuel moisture codes are numerical indices used to estimate the moisture content of different layers of forest fuels and are widely applied to assess the ignition potential and behavior of wildfires. Terrain-corrected L-band ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery predicted the Drought Code (DC) and Duff Moisture Code (DMC) of the Canadian Forest Fire Danger Rating System in mountainous forests of British Columbia. Random forest regression models were developed using backscatter, decomposition parameters, and polarimetric discriminators obtained from forest (high-biomass, conifer-dominated), sparse (medium-biomass, open canopy), and unforested (low-biomass, herbaceous-dominated) fuel types near weather stations. Out-of-bag predicted values were compared against weather station-derived values. Models trained using SAR data predicted the DC with moderate accuracy in sparse (R2 = 0.49, RMSE = 165.65) and forest sites (R2 = 0.39, RMSE = 173.80), and with low accuracy in unforested sites (R2 = 0.15, RMSE = 205.96). Models trained using SAR data predicted the DMC with moderate accuracy in sparse (R2 = 0.64, RMSE = 26.07) and unforested sites (R2 = 0.47, RMSE = 31.52), and with low accuracy in forest sites (R2 = 0.12, RMSE = 40.71). Incorporating SAR data and day of year (DOY) improved the accuracy of DC models. Errors in both DC and DMC increased when models were evaluated with SAR data from weather stations not used in training, suggesting limited spatial transferability beyond training weather stations. Results suggest that terrain-corrected L-band polarimetric SAR has potential for predicting fuel moisture in mountainous and forested environments. Differences in surface and soil conditions across the fire environment must be accounted for to improve the spatial transferability of the models.

title: Machine Learning-Based Bias Correction Scheme for FY-4A AGRI Radiance Assimilation and Its Impact on Typhoon Forecasting
summary: Data assimilation generally assumes that observation-minus-background (OMB) departures follow an unbiased Gaussian distribution. Therefore, bias correction (BC) is essential for the effective assimilation of satellite radiances. This study applies four machine learning (ML) approaches to reduce systematic biases in clear-sky observations from the water-vapor-sensitive channels 9 and 10 of the Fengyun-4A (FY-4A) Advanced Geosynchronous Radiation Imager (AGRI). These methods include random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and the Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN). The machine-learning-based bias correction (MLBC) methods are evaluated for Typhoon In-Fa (2021) using the Weather Research and Forecasting Data Assimilation (WRFDA) system. Experiments without BC and with conventional variational bias correction (VarBC) are designed for comparison. Compared with VARBC, the four MLBC methods better capture nonlinear OMB biases and improve the statistical distributions of the departures. They produce more symmetric OMB distributions for channel 9 and distributions closer to the Gaussian distribution for channel 10, with smaller OMB STDVs and RMSEs than VARBC over both land and ocean for channel 10. After assimilation, KANBC produces the smallest OMA STDV and RMSE for both channels. For the Typhoon In-Fa case examined here, KANBC yields the smallest track errors among the experiments. In particular, KAN-based BC reduces the anomalously strong positive 500 hPa geopotential height increments over the continental high pressure and western North Pacific subtropical high pressure. The resulting initial conditions improve the environmental steering flow and reduce the northwestward track bias. Channel sensitivity experiments were further conducted for water-vapor-sensitive channels 9 and 10 of the FY-4A AGRI using the KAN-based BC method. The results show that single-channel assimilation performs better than dual-channel assimilation. Assimilating channel 10 alone produces the smallest track errors and lower analysis RMSEs relative to ERA5 than assimilating both channels.

title: Advancing remote sensing of carbon fractions in coastal waters: retrieval algorithms and optical proxies for Sentinel-2 MSI and Sentinel-3 OLCI
summary: A thorough understanding of the global carbon pools and cycle is essential for understanding and predicting the effects of climate change. Coastal waters play a key role in the global carbon cycle but remain poorly understood due to their optical complexity, high spatial variability, and sensitivity to climate change. Satellite remote sensing data can provide high spatial and temporal resolution for carbon monitoring at local, regional, and global scales. This study estimates the potential of Sentinel-2 MSI (S2) and Sentinel-3 OLCI (S3) for mapping carbon fractions in coastal waters. In situ hyperspectral reflectance measurements and concentrations of different carbon fractions, namely Total Organic Carbon (TOC), Dissolved Organic Carbon (DOC), Particulate Organic Carbon (POC), and Dissolved Inorganic Carbon (DIC), were used. Bio-optical and physical water parameters, as well as carbon fractions, were measured in the coastal areas of the eastern Baltic Sea from 2023 to 2024. In situ reflectance spectra were recalculated to S2 and S3 band reflectance using their respective spectral response functions. Regression models, including linear regression and machine learning methods, were developed and validated against in situ data to estimate carbon fractions. For S2, the combinations of green and red or red-edge bands achieved the best performance in carbon retrieval, with R 2 values of 0.67, 0.64, and 0.56 for TOC, DOC, and DIC, respectively. The corresponding MAPE values ranged from 14% to 18%, and biases were close to zero. Slightly higher accuracies were obtained with S3 simulations. The S3 models that used reflectance at 490, 620, and 665 nm produced the most accurate estimates for both TOC ( R 2 = 0.71) and DOC ( R 2 = 0.67). For DIC, the best predictive model combined information from 510, 665, and 709 nm bands, achieving R 2 of 0.62. Among the tested optical proxies, CDOM absorption at 443 nm showed the most consistent relationship with TOC, DOC, and DIC ( R 2 = 0.56–0.30). The study represents a significant step forward in the remote sensing of coastal waters, and if adopted, the proposed carbon-fraction products could enable substantial progress across various fields, from carbon-cycle research to monitoring and policymaking.

title: Uncertainty as the key to interoperability: Traceable frameworks for space-based imaging spectroscopy
summary: By the end of this decade, several space agencies and commercial operators will develop and launch the next generation of space-based Earth observation satellites. This paper focuses on imaging spectroradiometers, which measure solar radiation reflected by the Earth’s surface across the ultra-violet, visible and short-wave infrared spectral ranges using hyperspectral sensors. To enable interoperable use of datasets from this growing constellation of sensors, it is essential to understand and manage differences between the measurements of the same target under similar conditions. These differences arise from multiple factors: real variations due to instrument design (e.g., differing spectral responses or viewing geometries), differences in Level 1 processing approaches based on pre-flight and post-launch calibration strategies, differences in higher-level processing into biophysical quantities, and any residual biases between sensors caused by measurement or processing errors — some of which may not be fully captured in reported uncertainties. A consistent approach to the analysis and documentation of uncertainties supports intercomparison between datasets. By assessing whether measurements agree within the expected uncertainty associated with the comparison, or identifying and quantifying systematic deviations when they do not, it becomes possible to validate interoperability and diagnose discrepancies. This paper outlines key concepts for harmonising uncertainty analysis and reporting techniques across missions, including the use of structured uncertainty propagation frameworks such as uncertainty trees. The goal is to initiate a roadmap for understanding and quantifying uncertainties in a way that facilitates robust intercomparison of multiple space-based imaging spectroradiometer measurements.

title: PACE hyperspectral observations enable a new paradigm for global mapping of terrestrial gross primary production
summary: Accurate quantification of terrestrial gross primary production (GPP) is fundamental to understanding plant productivity, ecosystem function, and carbon-climate feedbacks. Existing approaches typically rely on meteorological, soil, and other ancillary inputs, which introduce substantial uncertainties at regional to global scales. NASA's Plankton, Aerosol, Cloud, ocean Ecosystem (PACE) mission, carrying the Ocean Color Instrument (OCI), provides the first contiguous global hyperspectral observations from space. Using 122 spectral bands from PACE, we developed a data-driven framework based on partial least squares regression to generate an 8-day global GPP product. The model achieves a robust performance (R 2 = 0.71, RMSE = 1.93 gC m −2 d −1 ), comparable to models that incorporate meteorological drivers, and outperforms approaches based on broadband reflectance or vegetation indices. PACE-derived GPP showed broad spatial correspondence with solar-induced fluorescence (SIF), including hotspots across high productivity regions such as the U.S. Corn Belt, the Amazon and Congo basins, and the Indo-Gangetic and North China Plains. This strong spatial coherence supports the physiological relevance of the PACE retrievals. Our results demonstrate that hyperspectral observations provide a direct, observation-driven framework for estimating plant productivity at the global scale, opening new opportunities for monitoring vegetation responses to environmental change.
